title: Best Hyeon Burst loadout in Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer
content:
The Hyeon Burst is one of the very few burst-fire weapons in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , but this means it can be quite lethal when paired with the right loadout. Fortunately, the Hyeon Burst has some great attachments that boost its key stats, making it deadly in the right hands if you can hit your shots. While it may not have the same fully-automatic feel as other assault rifles, such as the M4 , if you have a fast trigger finger, you’ll be unstoppable with the Hyeon Burst in multiplayer.

Below, you can see the strongest loadout for the Hyeon Burst in MW4.

The Hyeon Burst fully relies on your ability to hit shots when burst-firing, as missing shots brings your TTK way down. By default, the Hyeon Burst leaves something to be desired compared to the stats of other ARs, so we’re going to improve the weapon across the board to make it more competitive.

Here’s our recommended loadout for the Hyeon Burst:

For this Hyeon Burst loadout, we’re looking to improve the AR’s overall accuracy while speeding up its TTK in the process. Prioritizing recoil control allows the weapon to stay on target more consistently, but you also want a faster fire rate to ensure you’re killing enemies as quickly as possible. We’ve also slightly boosted mobility with the laser for any close-range gunfights you happen to get into.

This loadout also uses the Slimline Elite optic, but if you aren’t a fan of that sight, you can replace it with something else, like the SZ Prima-4 Dot.

title: Overwatch Hero 55: Hudson changes from support to DPS omnic detective
content:
Overwatch game director Aaron Keller and associate game director Alec Dawson just announced that the new omnic detective will be a damage hero instead of a support. Overwatch Hero 55’s name will also be Hudson.

Originally announced as a support hero, Overwatch’s omnic detective will soon debut as a damage hero instead of a support in Season 6. Dawson revealed this change during a Twitch livestream with content creators Emongg and Flats.

“The core mechanic and the thing that we were really falling in love with on this hero didn’t really match with being a support, and we kind of leaned into the things we loved the most about the hero, and it definitely fits DPS a lot better,” Dawson said . “So we’re really excited for him pretty soon. He has a very fun accent, I’ll say that. I’m allowed to say that.”

Prior to this change, a tarot card handed out in person at BlizzCon 2026 pointed to the omnic detective being a support hero .

After this explanation, Keller accidently revealed that the omnic detective’s name will be Hudson. “There was a bit of a pivot on Hudson,” he said before realizing it.

Shortly after this, the official Overwatch account on social media made an announcement to confirm the name.

title: BETBY becomes first company to receive ESIC’s CPU v CPU Gold Standard accreditation
content:
The Esports Integrity Commission (ESIC) has awarded BETBY the first CPU v CPU Gold Standard accreditation , recognizing the betting provider’s effort and commitment to comply with ESIC’s integrity requirements for automated esports competitions.

The certification follows an on-site audit, an assessment of additional evidence, and an independent audit review conducted in August 2026. BETBY will also undergo annual audit reviews to maintain its accreditation.

The recognition marks the first time an organization has met the requirements under ESIC’s newly introduced framework, which aims to strengthen trust in automated esports competitions used in betting markets.

The CPU v CPU Gold Standard was introduced to address integrity concerns surrounding automated esports competitions, where match outcomes are generated by software rather than human players. Examples include virtual football and basketball matches, which have gained popularity in betting markets because they are available around the clock and typically take only a few minutes to finish.

According to ESIC, the framework establishes 17 mandatory control areas covering the systems responsible for generating and validating match results, the infrastructure supporting these competitions, and the personnel authorized to operate or modify them.

These requirements provide a basis for independently assessing how automated competitions are managed and whether the necessary safeguards are in place to protect their integrity.

title: Laocorn Gaudeamus enters FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves
content:
SNK Corporation has announced the release date for Laocorn Gaudeamus in FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves.

Part of Season Pass 3, Laocorn becomes a playable FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves character on Nov. 19. He also arrives with his own Episodes of South Town stories and Arcade Mode.

Known as a major antagonist in the 1994 film FATAL FURY: The Motion Picture , Laocorn previously fought Terry Bogard over the Armor of Mars. Now, decades later, he is closer than ever to completing the set. After all, the final piece is up for grabs in South Town’s King of Fighters (KOF) tournament.

In terms of what Laocorn brings to the KOF showdown, SNK Corporation released a preview of his moves in the video below. The video also revealed Brandon Loera as the new fighter’s English voice actor. Laocorn’s Japanese voice actor, meanwhile, is Shin-ichiro Miki.

The arrival of Laocorn on Nov. 19 means six confirmed releases for 2026 so far. Prior to him, Rick Strowd, Duck King, Kim Kaphwan, Manjiro “Mikey” Sano, and Ken “Draken” Ryuguji joined this year’s roster as DLC fighters . Meanwhile, Reina from TEKKEN 8 is slated to release sometime this December.

That’s all for now. Are you ready to duke it out as Laocorn in FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves? Stick around on esports.gg for more news and updates .

title: Chovy, enfin en finale des Worlds : « Je veux profiter de ce moment »
content:
C’est un moment que Jeong « Chovy » Ji-hoon attend depuis le début de sa carrière. Après huit participations aux championnats du monde, le joueur de Gen.G a enfin décroché son billet pour la grande finale des Worlds 2026. Une qualification obtenue face à Invictus Gaming, au terme d’une rencontre durant laquelle les Sud-Coréens ont dû s’adapter au style particulièrement collectif de leurs adversaires. Dans un entretien accordé à Inven Global , Chovy est notamment revenu sur les ajustements réalisés en pleine partie pour répondre aux regroupements incessants de la formation chinoise.

Désormais, tous les regards sont tournés vers la finale, où Gen.G retrouvera le vainqueur du duel entre T1 et Bilibili Gaming. Deux adversaires que Chovy refuse de départager. « Dès que T1 est dans l’équation, il est impossible de faire des pronostics » , explique-t-il. En attendant de connaître son opposant, le midlaner compte surtout peaufiner sa préparation, malgré l’absence d’équipes disponibles pour disputer des scrims. Le travail se concentrera notamment sur la SoloQ et l’analyse des drafts, un domaine dans lequel il estime que Gen.G possède actuellement un avantage sur ses concurrents.

Au-delà de l’enjeu sportif, cette première finale mondiale représente un accomplissement particulièrement émouvant pour Chovy. Après tant d’années à poursuivre ce rêve, le Sud-Coréen veut éviter de se laisser submerger par la pression. « J’ai atteint la finale après huit ans, et je pense que c’est un moment qui ne se reproduira peut-être jamais. Je ne veux pas laisser la nervosité ou l’anxiété me gâcher un moment aussi important » , confie-t-il, avant d’ajouter : « Je veux profiter de ce moment qui n’arrivera peut-être qu’une seule fois et remporter le championnat. »

Le joueur a également profité de cet entretien pour adresser un message touchant à sa mère, qui l’accompagne depuis ses débuts. « Même si je ne l’exprime pas beaucoup extérieurement, ma mère m’aide énormément. Parfois, elle me sert de modèle dans ma vie » , raconte-t-il, avant de la remercier avec une certaine pudeur. À une victoire du titre mondial, Chovy n’a désormais plus qu’une marche à gravir pour transformer huit années d’efforts en consécration historique.

title: Total Gaming, Payal Gaming and Sharkshe Join YouTube’s 24-Hour GTA 6 Launch Livestream
content:
Indian creators Total Gaming, Payal Gaming and Sharkshe are among more than 30 streamers named for YouTube’s 24-hour Grand Theft Auto 6 launch livestream. YouTube announced the broadcast on 12 November as part of a launch partnership with Rockstar Games . The stream marks the release of GTA VI on 19 November. YouTube has not said how long each creator will appear or what each will stream.

Total Gaming, run by Ajay “Ajjubhai”, is one of India’s largest gaming channels and built its audience on Garena Free Fire. Payal Dhare, known as Payal Gaming, is among the most-subscribed female gaming creators in India. Sharkshe streams BGMI and joined Team Apex Gaming as a creator after Jonathan’s exit from GodLike.

the biggest launch of all time deserves the biggest livestream. 24 hours. 11/18. 11pm ET. YouTube. https://t.co/tFeDr8AQNI pic.twitter.com/vzDemGAMfe

The broadcast opens with a pre-show hosted by RDCWorld. The 24-hour main stream follows and runs through launch day. It will be hosted on YouTube’s own channel, and viewers can also reach it through a GTA VI-themed YouTube logo on the homepage. YouTube produced the stream with Entropico.

The named creators come from more than a dozen countries. They include Caylus, Zhong, Kat Buno, Jelly, Rivers, Jake Baldino, Cinna, Loserfruit, JuanSGuarnizo, GamerCosta, Windah Basudara, Samira Close and Kinda Funny Games. YouTube said the full line-up includes “and more”, so further names may be added.

YouTube is adding five limited-edition GTA VI Live gifts, including a “Wanted Stars” animation. Eligible viewers can claim one while supplies last. A Shorts effect called “GTAVI: Visit Vice City” places users into scenes from the game. The official GTA VI soundtrack, which includes Morgan Wallen’s “Last Thing You Need”, will feature on the YouTube Music homepage during launch week.

title: Genshin Impact Cheater Selling Paid Stygian Onslaught Carries Reportedly Arrested While Meeting Customers
content:
Chinese police allegedly detained a Genshin Impact player who allegedly used cheats to sell paid Stygian Onslaught clears, while the player was meeting customers in a clothing store. The arrest has not been confirmed by police or by HoYoverse, the game’s developer. The player’s name, the city and the date of the arrest have not been disclosed.

Security camera images from inside the store , dated 3 November, circulated online alongside the claims. A second image showed a Chinese-language apology to HoYoverse on a phone screen. Neither the police nor HoYoverse has commented publicly on the case.

In the apology, the player admitted to posting videos of themselves “using cheats in Genshin Impact” without authorisation. The player said the actions “seriously violated” the official rules of miHoYo and Genshin Impact, which prohibit cheating. The player has since deleted the posts that advertised the service.

The player promoted the service through videos on Bilibili that showed the cheats in use. The videos directed viewers to a store on Xianyu, a Chinese second-hand marketplace, that sold the boosting service. Prices for the service have not been disclosed.

Stygian Onslaught is a combat challenge in Genshin Impact made up of three timed battles. Higher difficulty levels add tougher enemies and stricter time limits, and the mode rewards players who clear them quickly. The allegations first surfaced on the Chinese gaming forum NGA before spreading on other platforms.

HoYoverse said in March 2026 that it removed more than one million illegal links and pieces of content during 2025, including cheat software and pirated resources. In 2023, the company threatened legal action against cheaters after malicious plug-ins affected other players’ accounts.

title: Naughty Dog’s Intergalactic is playable and in final polish, Druckmann says
content:
Naughty Dog's Neil Druckmann says that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet has reached the final stage of production, with the game now playable, Inven Global reported. It's the first proper status check we’ve had on the PS5 project since its reveal, and it seems that all systems are go.

Druckmann, the studio head and the game's director and writer were speaking at Comic Creators Block Party 2026. Host and comedian Patton Oswalt asked for more details but Druckmann was keen to keep his lips sealed where the story is concerned.

"We've only teased it, so I can't talk too much about it," he said before adding "we're kind of like at the last stages of production, where we can play it, and we're refining it and polishing it, and I can't wait to show it to the world."

While he may be resistant to saying much more at the moment, Druckmann reassured Oswalt and everyone else that the studio will reveal more next year. "We're going to show gameplay, more of the story," he revealed, which fits an earlier September update when Naughty Dog said it needed "to cook for just a little bit longer."

No release date or window has been given, though, and for now only PS5 is a confirmed platform, where Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet will be published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.

Despite expressing reluctance to dive deeper into the story, Druckmann fed fans a few crumbs when he described the new game as a mix of Jak and Daxter, The Last of Us and action-adventure title Uncharted. He says the team were eager to recreate the sci-fi and fantasy of Jak and Daxter, while mixing in the pulp adventure of Uncharted, before ramping things up with the punishing drama of The Last of Us . If all this is accurate, it’ll be the studio’s first sci-fi-tinged outing since Jak and Daxter.

title: BLAST Rivals Fall 2026 Turns Hong Kong Into Final Major Test
content:
BLAST Rivals Fall 2026 is underway in Hong Kong, bringing together eight Counter-Strike 2 teams for one of the final major international tests before the PGL Singapore Major.

The tournament runs from November 11 to November 15 and features a $1 million prize pool. Every participating team has already qualified for Singapore, which gives the event unusual significance: results in Hong Kong offer a direct look at how several Major contenders are performing immediately before the season’s biggest tournament.

The field is split into two groups of four.

Group A features FURIA, Vitality, Falcons and Legacy, while Group B includes Spirit, G2, MOUZ and FUT Esports.

The format combines double-elimination groups with a single-elimination playoff stage.

With every team already qualified for Singapore, BLAST Rivals is less about qualification pressure and more about proving current form before the Major.

title: Jonathan Calls Kronten’s Allegations “Completely Wrong” in First Response to GodLike Dispute
content:
Jonathan “Jonathan” Amaral, founder of Team Apex Gaming, has called the allegations made against him by GodLike Esports owner Chetan “Kronten” Chandgude “completely wrong”. He spoke during a livestream on Kick on 12 November, his first spoken response since the dispute began. Jonathan said he would not address most of the claims in detail. He did not respond point by point to the ownership or salary figures Kronten gave.

Jonathan said he did not like getting involved in such matters and that the statements made “no sense”. He said he had “no idea” what some of the claims referred to. He added that he would only address “a few things”, and that one claim had made him laugh.

The one claim Jonathan addressed directly concerned his emotions after poor results. Kronten had said on his stream that Jonathan appeared upset on camera after defeats but behaved differently once the cameras were off. Jonathan said anyone who plays sport or esports and comes close to a goal without reaching it would be upset. He said players who lose “won’t dance” afterwards.

He also made a sarcastic remark about money while discussing the claim. Jonathan suggested that Kronten might not have emotions, before adding a reference to “crores of rupees”. He did not name Kronten at any point in the comments.

The response followed an Instagram story Jonathan posted after Kronten’s stream, which read “I choose me, I’m sorry”. The line is from Kendrick Lamar’s song “Mirror”. Jonathan did not explain the story or say whether it was a reply to Kronten.

Kronten made the allegations during a livestream in early November. He said management never benched Jonathan at BGIS 2026, and that Jonathan sat out the first day of the Survival Stage because of a shoot. As we covered in our report on Kronten’s claim that GodLike never benched Jonathan , Jonathan had said at the time that the decision was taken in the team’s interest.

title: TenZ Is Back! Valorant Legend Joins T1 After 2 Years Away
content:
The king is back. TenZ, one of Valorant's biggest names, has left the streaming desk and joined T1's active roster. After two years away from the pro scene, he plays again from 2027.

T1 announced the move on X. The organization called TenZ a living legend of Valorant and said a new chapter starts now. It added that it is ready to make history with him and asked fans to give him a warm welcome.

TenZ will play in VCT Pacific beginning with the 2027 Kickoff. Until now he had been part of T1 as a streamer.

The Canadian has not played professionally since 2024. In 2025 he made a few stand-in appearances for Cubert Academy, then put his focus on content creation.

On October 21 he posted "LFT" on X, short for looking for team. The post set off reports that a comeback was close. Fans guessed. T1 has now settled it.

TenZ is a two-time Masters champion. He won Masters Reykjavik in 2021 and Masters Madrid in 2024, both with Sentinels. Few names in Valorant carry that much weight.

title: RNTX Announces New Valorant Roster With Hoax, hellff, DcRulz, venka and Lightningfast
content:
Revenant XSpark (RNTX) has announced a new five-player Valorant roster of Aman “Hoax” Yadav, Sagnik “hellff” Roy, Daivik “DcRulz” Chauhan, Venkatesh “venka” Sharma and Abhirup “Lightningfast” Paul Choudhury. The line-up brings together two Indian cores that finished first and third at VCT Challengers 2026 South Asia Split 2 in June.

Hoax and venka are the two players staying from the previous RNTX roster. Lightningfast, hellff and DcRulz join together. The three played as a unit at Gods Reign and then under the NSP tag, where they won Challengers South Asia Split 2. As per our sources, Shravana “Techno” Kumar Sahoo will stay on as the substitute. He joined RNTX with Hoax and venka on 18 February. The organisation has not confirmed his status publicly.

As per our sources, Hoax will make the calls for the team and share the initiator and flex roles with hellff. Lightningfast is expected to play controller and anchor sites. venka stays on duelist, and DcRulz is set to play sentinel and flex. hellff is expected to fill whatever roles are left in each composition.

venka’s long-term future with the side is less certain. TalkEsport’s sources said the 20-year-old plans to go abroad for studies in January 2027, which would make him a short-term signing. This has not been confirmed by venka or RNTX.

Lightningfast, 25, has won four Challengers South Asia events since the start of 2025. He spent almost four years at Global Esports between November 2020 and August 2024, winning the Skyesports Champions Series in 2022. At Velocity Gaming he won Challengers 2025 South Asia Split 1, Split 3 and the Grand Final, beating S8UL 3–1 in the Grand Final.

hellff, 27, started out in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive with Global Esports before moving to Valorant in 2020. He has since played for Velocity Gaming, Team Mahi, True Rippers, Orangutan and S8UL Esports. At S8UL he was part of the side that finished second at Challengers 2025 South Asia Split 3 and the Grand Final, losing both finals to Velocity.

title: VALORANT Bunker Returns to Mumbai on 22 November at Ballard Pier, With Rolling Loud India and Red Bull on Board
content:
VALORANT Bunker, Riot Games’ music and community night for Indian players, is returning to Mumbai on 22 November 2026, this time at Ballard Pier in the south of the city. Riot’s VALORANT India and South Asia team confirmed the date on 12 November with a poster that lists Red Bull, Rolling Loud India and JioBLAST among the event’s partners. “The game, the music, the community,” the official post reads, and Riot teased the comeback earlier the same day with a short video captioned “BUNKER is back”. Riot has not yet announced the line-up, timings or how fans can get in.

The game, the music, the community. It's all coming together on Nov 22nd. pic.twitter.com/mJbHWe9J7Q

The first VALORANT Bunker took place in Mumbai on 27 November 2024, with electronic artists Ritviz and Gravero on the bill. That night also gave fans the first live preview of “Gotcha Back”, the anthem that Riot and the music collective ARB4 released as a full music video in December 2024. ARB4 had earlier made “RAJA”, the theme song for Harbor, VALORANT’s first Indian agent. Riot first announced that 2024 Bunker on 12 November 2024, exactly two years before this year’s reveal.

This year’s poster also carries a hint about the headline agent. Its artwork shows a white-haired agent in pink tones that closely resembles Hush, the telekinetic Duelist Riot added in patch 13.09 in late October. Riot’s first teaser line for the event, “No need to be Hush about this one”, points the same way. Riot has not said whether Hush will feature in any in-game tie-in or event reward.

This year’s edition moves Bunker to Ballard Pier, in the Ballard Estate area of south Mumbai beside the city’s port. Riot has been teasing the return for weeks, including a 7 November post that told fans to close their seat trays because “BUNKER is back”. It has not said how many people the venue will hold or whether entry will be free.

Bunker is part of a wider push by Riot to connect VALORANT with India’s music scene. In November 2025, VALORANT ran an experience zone at the India debut of the hip-hop festival Rolling Loud in Navi Mumbai, with karaoke pods, quick duels and live art. “It’s the perfect stage for us to meet players where they are,” Arun Rajappa, Riot Games India’s director of publishing, said at the time. Rolling Loud India’s logo on this year’s Bunker poster suggests that relationship has carried over into Riot’s own event.

title: BLAST Rivals Season 2 2026: Day 2 Results & Highlights
content:
Following an action-packed Day 1, Day 2 of the BLAST Rivals Season 2 2026 has yielded the highly anticipated single-elimination playoffs. With the interesting format of BLAST Rivals, only two teams, namely Legacy and FUT, will be heading home as others prepare for the quarter-finals tomorrow.

. @FalconsEsport secure their spot in the playoffs here in Hong Kong #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/Ew25qVlwGn

Starting with a 5-0 scoreline, the Falcons managed to set a dominant tone to the series early on before Legacy salvaged the half by taking 5 rounds, trailing by 2 rounds at the break. Winning the pistol, the second half saw Legacy manage to narrow down the lead before Falcons converted the lead. Winning on the weaker buy enabled them to hit double digits, leaving Legacy to play chase. Legacy’s poorly orchestrated offence failed to manage anything significant as they watched Falcons effortlessly close the opening map of the day.

Losing on Falcons’ map, Legacy failed to set a strong start on their own map pick of Mirage as their poor offensive display from the first map came back to haunt them. Falcons’ 9-round defensive performance gave them a solid lead to switch sides with confidence. With a big margin to their name, the Falcons dropped a few rounds but closed eventually, eliminating Legacy in the process with a 13-6 win as m0NESY dropped another chart-topping performance.

A 13-0 TO SECURE THE SEMI-FINAL SPOT #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/G035kkZJmV

A statement start on FURIA’s map pick against Vitality enabled them to go 11-1 up as the Brazilian side looked helpless on their offence, having secured a single round. Switching sides, the FURIA defence pulled 4 rounds, but that barely helped, as winning two back-to-back rounds saw Vitality push the opening map over the line.

title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO After 33 Years; Colette Kress Named Interim Chief
content:
Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and turned a graphics-card maker for PC gamers into the company at the centre of the AI boom, is no longer its chief executive. On Thursday, 12 November, Nvidia announced that Huang has resigned as president, CEO and a member of the board , effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.

The announcement ends a week in which the pressure on Huang kept building. It started with questions over his relationship with an executive whom US officials suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. Then came his own written admission to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, followed by fresh allegations about a second relationship, this time inside Nvidia. The board met on Wednesday night to decide his future, and the meeting ran into the evening. By Thursday morning in California, the most famous leather jacket in tech had left the building. Nvidia’s statement gives no reason for the departure, although the timing leaves little room for interpretation.

The unravelling began in late October, when The New York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data-centre company Megaspeed. Megaspeed is an Nvidia customer, and it was already under investigation by US and Singaporean authorities over suspected chip-export violations. According to the Times, a US intelligence memo had alleged that she was working for China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has dismissed those claims as baseless, and Nvidia’s first response was that Huang’s interactions with her were “not unusual or unexpected” for a CEO who meets customers.

That line did not hold for long. On Sunday, 8 November, Huang wrote to employees admitting that he had been unfaithful to his wife of 40 years and apologising. The note named no one. On the same day, Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into whether he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. It also said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised. Two days later, the independent directors brought in former acting US Attorney Joon H. Kim and his firm to run the review. Then, on Wednesday, the Times reported a second affair, citing current and former employees, this time with a senior Nvidia executive who reports directly to Huang. Neither Nvidia nor Huang has confirmed that report. Within hours, The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to remove him.

Washington was also closing in. Three House Republican committee chairmen, John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford, had asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on his ties to Alice Huang. They also warned that a subpoena could follow if he did not respond. Meanwhile, Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the administration to preserve Nvidia’s China-related records. President Donald Trump stood by Huang throughout, calling him “an honorable guy” and saying he should stay on. In the end, however, the decision belonged to Nvidia’s board, and Huang had little power to resist it. He owns roughly 3.6% of the company, so unlike founders at Meta or SpaceX, he had no majority voting control to fall back on.

Colette Kress has been Nvidia’s executive vice president and CFO since September 2013. Before that, she spent nearly 25 years in finance at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments. She keeps the CFO job alongside the top role. In Nvidia’s statement, she said she is committed to “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.” The board also named Harvey C. Jones, a former CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys, as the company’s first-ever chair. That is a telling change for a company that, until this week, had no board chair at all. According to Jones, the board has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team” and expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to carry on without interruption. The search for a permanent CEO will look at both internal and external candidates.

title: Xbox Cloud Gaming Free Tier Is Live: Session Limits, Ads and Prices
content:
The Xbox Cloud Gaming free tier is now live for most players around the world. Xbox rolled out the ad-supported option on November 11, 2026, after testing it for several months. Players can stream select games from their library and some free-to-play titles without a Game Pass subscription. Each session starts with ads, and session time limits apply.

This article covers how the free tier works, the new Game Pass cloud limits, and Cloud Playtime prices.

Xbox announced the free version of Xbox Cloud Gaming in July. At that stage, it was a test for Xbox Insiders. As of November 11, it has reached the vast majority of Xbox users.

The free tier lets players stream select games from their own library, along with select free-to-play games. Xbox has not said which games qualify. Players need to check the supported cloud library for the current list.

You now have more ways to stream and play your favorite games. Purchase ad-free cloud playtime, get monthly cloud playtime with @XBOXGamePass , or stream your games for free with ad-supported cloud gaming. Choose your way to play: https://t.co/60P9n1npR5 pic.twitter.com/Lh8phIKBEF

Xbox shared the details in a post on X . It said players can stream select games for free by watching ads before each gaming session. After a session ends, players can watch another set of ads to start a new one.

title: Call of Duty Ranked Levels: Every Skill Division and What Carries Into a New Title
content:
Call of Duty ranked levels in mainline multiplayer Ranked Play run from Bronze to a Top 250 leaderboard finish. Black Ops 7 treats a new season differently depending on whether you finished below Platinum, and a new title begins its own progression. Warzone and Call of Duty Mobile have separate ranked systems.

Black Ops 7 Ranked Play has seven named Skill Divisions that group players by rank, followed by Top 250, a place on the leaderboard for the highest-ranked competitors. In order, the eight ladder positions are Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Crimson, Iridescent, and Top 250. Top 250 is a leaderboard position rather than another ordinary division to grind through. As a new player, you’ll receive a starting rank only after winning the required placement matches.

This is the Black Ops 7 multiplayer ladder; Warzone and Call of Duty Mobile use their own ranked systems.

Players in the Bronze division through Gold keep their rank and SR when a new season starts, but players in Platinum and above need a placement win. Rank is only part of what a profile carries, though: building one from scratch with the level, weapons, and camos you want takes a long run of matches. Players who would rather start from a finished profile can browse Call of Duty accounts on Skycoach , a marketplace where each Black Ops 7, Modern Warfare 4, or Warzone account listing shows whether it is ranked-ready, along with its level, Prestige, camo count, weapons, and the platforms it links to (PC, PlayStation, or Xbox). Skycoach has operated since 2020, and purchases come with buyer protection: a warranty period, a refund policy, and 24/7 support.

Black Ops 7 starts with placements. You must win three placement matches to receive a starting rank, and after each placement win, the Minimum Starting Rank updates to show a projection of where you’re expected to land.

After a Ranked Play win, you gain Skill Rating (SR), which sets your position on the ladder. The amount isn’t fixed: it depends on your match performance relative to the skill of the other players and the team’s margin of victory. The same factors affect SR deducted after a loss. As Activision’s ranked support page explains, the SR change depends on these match factors, so two wins during the same evening can award different amounts without an error in the display.

title: Alice Huang’s husband, a video game investor, introduced her to Jensen Huang, report suggests
content:
Jensen Huang was introduced to Alice Huang by her own husband, according to a new report by the Wall Street Journal’s Lingling Wei. The husband, a Chinese businessman, had known the Nvidia chief executive for about a decade before making the introduction. When the two men first met in the 2010s, he was a private equity investor focused on video game companies, at a time when Nvidia was still best known for PC gaming graphics cards.

The Journal reports that he is also Alice Huang’s business partner, and that he appeared to accept her romantic relationship with Huang. According to people familiar with the couple, he spoke openly about her closeness to the Nvidia chief.

The report adds a new layer to a scandal that has already put Huang’s job at risk. Huang admitted to an affair in a letter to staff on 8 November, without naming the person involved. Reports have since linked him to Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore firm Megaspeed, whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of gathering information for China. Nvidia’s board is reportedly preparing to remove him , although it has not announced a decision, and no charges have been reported against Alice Huang.

The Journal’s account places the start of the story in the games business. According to the report, the husband got to know Huang while investing in video game companies, years before Nvidia’s data centre chips made it the most valuable chip company in the world. Over the past decade, the couple then moved between business ventures in video game companies, pharmaceutical takeovers and cloud computing, the Journal says. The report does not give an exact date for when Huang and Alice Huang first met.

Video games also run through the wider Megaspeed story. Megaspeed, where Alice Huang worked, was set up in Singapore in 2023 as an offshore unit of 7Road, according to a New York Times investigation. The parent company is a Chinese games and cloud firm, best known for browser games such as DDTank and Wartune. That background, along with its purchases of billions of dollars of Nvidia hardware, is part of why Megaspeed sits at the centre of the scandal . The Journal’s report does not link the husband to Megaspeed or 7Road.

TalkEsport is not naming the husband, who is a private individual, although the Journal identifies him. The report relies on people familiar with the couple, and TalkEsport has not found any public comment from him or from Alice Huang. Nvidia previously described Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang as “not unusual”, saying he meets thousands of customer executives every year. Beijing has rejected the espionage claims as smears against China.

title: GTA 6 Release Time for All Regions: When GTA 6 Unlocks Worldwide
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI unlocks at midnight local time on 19 November in every region, on both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar Games is using a rolling regional release rather than a single global launch. New Zealand is first, at 11:00 UTC on 18 November. The US West Coast is last, at 08:00 UTC on 19 November, a gap of 21 hours.

The table shows when GTA VI unlocks in major cities, in local time and in UTC. Players in the same time zone as a listed city get the game at the same moment. In India, the game unlocks at 12:00 AM IST on 19 November, matching the PlayStation and Xbox India store listings.

The UTC times are our calculations based on midnight in each city, using standard time for 19 November. Countries that span several time zones, such as Australia, Brazil, Mexico and the US, unlock at local midnight in each zone. Rockstar has not published an official city-by-city unlock table.

The game unlocks automatically for players who pre-ordered digitally and finished the pre-load. Pre-loading opened on 10 November, and the game needs up to 212 GB of free space, as Rockstar’s pre-load FAQ states. Players who have not pre-loaded must download the full game after it unlocks. That can take hours on slower connections, as we covered in our report on GTA 6 pre-load times and file size .

Retail boxes contain a download code rather than a disc. Owners of physical editions still need to download the game, and Rockstar has not said whether any stores will open at midnight. GTA VI is available only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S at launch. Xbox One owners can play through Xbox Cloud Gaming, as we covered in our report on GTA 6 coming to Xbox One through the cloud .

Some players plan to switch their console region to New Zealand to start 21 hours earlier. Rockstar has not commented on the practice. The method differs between PS5 and Xbox, as we covered in our report on playing GTA 6 early with the New Zealand trick . Rockstar has not announced a PC version or a PC release date.

title: Sky Esports Win G2 x PUBG MOBILE Community Challenge on a Dust II-Inspired Map, Undisputed
content:
Amateur squad Sky Esports has won the G2 x PUBG MOBILE Community Challenge, a tournament played on a custom map inspired by Counter-Strike’s Dust II inside PUBG MOBILE. The team beat Star Dust Esports 2-0 in the best-of-three grand final over the weekend of 7 and 8 November, and took home €500 in cash, a €125 Amazon gift card and G2 merchandise.

Twenty-five teams entered the event, which was open only to amateur players and ran in a round-based bomb-defusal mode rather than PUBG MOBILE’s usual battle royale. The winners are not to be confused with Skyesports, the Indian tournament organiser.

The tournament opened on Saturday with best-of-one, single-elimination qualifiers, which left no room for an off day. With 25 teams chasing four semi-final places, a single defeat ended a team’s weekend. Sky Esports, WM Officials, Star Dust Esports and DMSXBIS came through to claim those slots. On Sunday, both semi-finals were played as best-of-three series, and both ended 2-0, with Sky Esports beating WM Officials and Star Dust Esports knocking out DMSXBIS.

The grand final was just as one-sided as the semi-finals. Sky Esports took the opening map and then won the second 6-1 to complete a 2-0 series win, according to the organisers. In the third-place match, played alongside the final, DMSXBIS beat WM Officials to finish on the podium. That means Sky Esports won every match it played across the two days, from the single-elimination qualifiers to the final.

Every team in the top four left with a prize. The cash prizes add up to the €1,000 prize pool that G2’s community account advertised when registration opened on 27 October. On top of that, the top three teams each received a €125 Amazon gift card and G2 merchandise, while fourth place took €125 in gift cards.

The custom map was the event’s main hook for Counter-Strike fans. Called PMG2, it was built in World of Wonder, the creation mode in PUBG MOBILE that lets players and partners design their own maps and game modes. Its layout is inspired by Dust II, one of the best-known maps in Counter-Strike’s history. To keep the Counter-Strike feel, teams played a classic bomb-defusal mode in which each player had a single life per match, according to the organisers.

title: LEC : kyeahoo prolonge avec la Karmine Corp (off.)
content:
La Karmine Corp tient sa première grande annonce de l’intersaison. Après plusieurs jours de rumeurs autour d’un possible départ, la structure française a officialisé ce jeudi la prolongation de Kang « kyeahoo » Ye-hoo pour 2027. Sur ses réseaux sociaux, le club a confirmé la nouvelle avec un message sans équivoque : « Le loup reste à la maison. » De quoi rassurer les supporters, alors que l’avenir du joueur était devenu l’un des principaux dossiers du mercato européen.

Auteur d’une solide saison 2026, conclue par un quart de finale aux Worlds, kyeahoo avait attiré l’attention de plusieurs formations étrangères. JD Gaming apparaissait notamment comme son principal prétendant, tandis que son entourage aurait réclamé une importante revalorisation salariale. Finalement, la KC est parvenue à conserver son midlaner, sans que les détails financiers de cette prolongation aient été dévoilés.

Cette signature permet désormais à la Karmine Corp de se concentrer sur les autres dossiers de son mercato. Le plus important concerne la jungle, où l’avenir de Yike reste incertain. Le Suédois, dont le contrat arrive à expiration, serait notamment en discussions avec Fnatic, même si une prolongation chez KC resterait envisageable.

En parallèle, la piste SkewMond prend de l’ampleur. Poussé vers la sortie par G2 Esports, le jungler français privilégierait le projet de la Karmine Corp malgré l’intérêt de Team Vitality. Son arrivée pourrait permettre au club de former un nouveau duo mid-jungle particulièrement prometteur avec kyeahoo. En attendant d’en savoir davantage, le Blue Wall peut déjà savourer une première victoire importante sur le marché des transferts.

title: Megaspeed Hires a US Law Firm to Count Its GPUs
content:
Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud company at the centre of the Nvidia espionage reports, has hired a US law firm to count its graphics processors and independently check whether it complied with US export controls. In an official statement dated 12 November on its website , chairman and chief executive Tan Yong Pong said the company had cooperated with inspections by the US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). He added that Megaspeed “stands ready to cooperate fully” with any other relevant US authority, and that it “welcomes appropriate government scrutiny”. It is the company’s first public statement since reports linked Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of gathering information for China.

The statement runs to four short paragraphs, signed by Tan as chairman and chief executive of Megaspeed International, and it leaves a great deal out. It does not mention Nvidia, Jensen Huang or Alice Huang, and it does not name the law firm, which it describes only as “a leading U.S. law firm”. It also gives no start date for the GPU census, and does not say whether the findings will be published. Nvidia’s board, meanwhile, has still not announced a decision on Huang, whom it is reportedly preparing to remove after a second affair report.

The tone is very different from Megaspeed’s previous public response. In December 2025, after a Bloomberg investigation into chip smuggling concerns, the company said it operated “fully within the bounds” of export control rules. It said inspections by BIS, Malaysia’s trade ministry and Nvidia itself had found no violations, and it did not rule out legal action against Bloomberg. The new statement repeats that Megaspeed cooperated with BIS inspections, but it makes no claim about what those inspections found.

BIS is the US agency that enforces export controls on advanced chips. Instead of repeating its earlier assurances, the company has handed an outside law firm the job of counting its GPUs and verifying its “export control compliance practices”. In export cases, the central question is usually where controlled chips ended up, and a full inventory is one way to answer it. US officials reportedly found Nvidia servers and GPUs still sealed in their crates when they inspected a Malaysian site linked to Megaspeed in late 2024. US lawmakers have since put the company’s Nvidia hardware imports at more than $4.6 billion.

Megaspeed itself grew out of the games industry. According to a New York Times investigation from October 2025, it was set up in Singapore in 2023 as an offshore unit of 7Road, a Chinese games and cloud company. The parent is backed by state investors and is best known for browser games such as DDTank and Wartune. That background, along with its rapid rise as an Nvidia customer, explains why Megaspeed sits at the centre of the Huang scandal . Its website now presents it as a specialised GPU cloud provider, advertising Nvidia GB200 NVL72 and HGX H100 systems from offices in Singapore and Jakarta.

US scrutiny of Megaspeed began more than a year before the Huang scandal. Senator Tom Cotton asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to investigate the company in an October 2025 letter , writing that it had received billions of dollars of US chips, “potentially violating U.S. export laws”. Megaspeed reportedly stopped ordering Nvidia hardware in July 2025, as investigations widened, and Alice Huang was reported to have left around the same time. Singapore police have said that their own inquiry concerns Megaspeed’s compliance with local law, not Alice Huang personally.

title: Elon Musk Says Hiring Jensen Huang “Would Be an Honour” Amid Nvidia Board Reports
content:
Elon Musk said on 11 November that hiring Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang “would be an honor”. Musk posted the reply on X under a post from the ZeroHedge account that read “Elon please hire Jensen”. He did not name a role or a company. Neither Musk, Huang nor Nvidia has said that any talks have taken place.

Musk’s reply came on the same day that reports said Nvidia’s board was preparing to meet and discuss Huang’s future at the company. Some of those reports said directors were considering removing him. Nvidia has not announced any change to its leadership. The board has not commented publicly on the reports, and Huang remains chief executive.

Musk runs Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. Several of his companies, including Tesla and xAI, use Nvidia’s AI computing hardware. His reply is not a job offer. Musk has not said which company Huang might join, or in what role. Huang has not responded to the post.

Nvidia shares closed at $173.73 on 11 November. They then fell $14.95, or 8.61%, to $158.78 in after-hours trading as the reports about the board spread. Nvidia has not said whether its directors met that day, or what they discussed.

Musk has commented on Huang before. Earlier this month his “you’re an asset” joke about Huang spread online, and we traced how Musk’s joke became a meme . We have also looked at who could replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia.

Huang, 63, told staff in an email on 8 November that he had had an extramarital affair. Nvidia’s board opened an investigation the same day, led by a committee of independent directors. It hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz on 10 November, as we covered in our report on the investigators leading the inquiry .

title: Krafton Releases Its Own On-Device AI Model, Raon-1 Nano, After Building PUBG Ally on Nvidia’s
content:
Krafton, the company behind PUBG: Battlegrounds and Battlegrounds Mobile India, has released Raon-1 nano, a small language model built for on-device inference. It has an effective 1.5 billion parameters and 3.1 billion in total, and the weights are on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence, which allows commercial use. Krafton says it was trained for multi-turn conversation, instruction following and tool calling, in Korean and English. For gamers, the relevant detail is that Krafton’s two shipped AI characters, PUBG Ally and inZOI’s Smart Zois, run on small models from Nvidia rather than on a model of Krafton’s own.

We’re releasing Raon-1 nano, an effective 1.5B dense LLM with per-layer embeddings and 3.1B total parameters. Our journey from PUBG Ally toward on-device LLMs continues. We pruned and distilled Raon-1 mini preview (30B-A4B) using our MoE-to-Dense approach, then further… pic.twitter.com/ydiQGrBlAd

KRAFTON AI, the company’s research arm, described the release as the next step in “our journey from PUBG Ally toward on-device LLMs”. Kangwook Lee, Krafton’s chief AI officer, said the company “finally” has “a better base model for our edge AI applications”, meaning models that run on local hardware such as a gaming PC. Krafton has not said which of its games will use Raon-1 nano, or when.

Krafton has shipped on-device AI in its games since inZOI entered early access in March 2025. Its optional Smart Zoi feature drives the city’s residents with a 0.5-billion-parameter Mistral NeMo Minitron model from Nvidia’s ACE platform, according to Nvidia , and it runs only on GeForce RTX graphics cards. PUBG Ally also uses Nvidia ACE, and its AI teammate Ella reached players in the Ally Duo beta on Sanhok in June 2026.

Krafton described Ally’s design in an engineering interview published by Nvidia . Its team first tested cloud-hosted models, but the combined network and inference latency made responses too slow for live squad play. It moved to Nvidia’s Mistral-NeMo-Minitron-2B, quantised it for client-side deployment and fitted it into the VRAM left over by PUBG, so Ally runs on GPUs with as little as 8GB. A separate Krafton research preprint put the median API cost of Claude Opus 4.8 at $7.10 per replayed match , and Krafton judged it impractical at scale.

The local approach still had limits in the beta. Ally Duo was restricted to PCs with GeForce RTX cards, and Krafton’s patch notes advised players who saw delayed responses to lower their graphics settings or resolution. That advice indicates the model and the game were competing for the same GPU resources.

title: Kick Free GTA 6: How to Get One of 10,000 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Codes
content:
Kick is giving away 10,000 digital copies of Grand Theft Auto VI Ultimate Edition through its Sunset Reward Case promotion. Viewers unlock a case by watching any stream on the platform for three hours. The promotion opened on 12 November and closes on 7 December. A case gives viewers a chance to win a code, and Kick does not guarantee a copy.

The steps are set out in Kick’s announcement of the Sunset Reward Case . No purchase, subscription or deposit is needed, and paying does not improve the odds.

New users can also open a free case once they finish Kick’s onboarding. Each valid entry has the same chance of winning, Kick says. Cases also contain emotes and badges. Codes are for PS5 or Xbox Series X|S, and Kick contacts winners at their registered email address.

Kick will not issue any codes before 19 November, the day GTA 6 launches, and some may arrive later. That means winners cannot use the promotion to pre-load the game. Selections stay provisional until Kick verifies each winner. Winners have at least 14 days to respond and confirm their details.

Xbox codes are open to eligible entrants worldwide, subject to local law and Microsoft’s restrictions. PS5 codes only work on PlayStation Network accounts registered in a list of supported countries, including the US, UK, Brazil, Japan and India. Choosing a region in the case does not change where a PSN account is registered. Kick says it owes no replacement if a winner picks the wrong console or region.

Kick runs the promotion on its own. It says it is not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive, and it does not share entrants’ personal data with Rockstar. The promoter is Kick Streaming Pty Ltd. Staff of Kick and Rockstar, and their immediate families, cannot enter.

title: Shreeman Legend Dismisses Team Apex Gaming BGMI Roster Disbandment Rumour
content:
The rumours of Team Apex’s Gaming’s Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) roster disbanding is spreading like a wildfire in the Indian esports community. Several social media handles have fuelled the speculation around the team’s future. However, Shreeman Legend, one of the founding members of Team Apex Gaming, has dismissed the rumour, assuring fans that the roster will remain intact for at least one year as per their contract.

When a viewer asked Shreeman whether Team Apex Gaming BGMI roster was on the verge of disbanding, he was quick to dismiss the rumours. He explained that whenever a roster is formed, a contract is signed and the team is binded by that contract. “Whenever a lineup is formed, especially in BGMI, it usually comes with a contract. The contract generally lasts for around six months to one year.”

Confirming the current roster’s contractual commitment, Shreeman clarified that the roster is signed for an entire year. “As far as the current team is concerned, the lineup we have right now is signed for one year. I don’t know where you’ve heard these rumours about a possible disbandment. I have no information about that. But for now, we are committed to this team for one year.”

He then assured fans that the team will keep playing together, “All the players you see here will continue playing together. After one year, the contract may get renewed. Whatever happens after that will be decided later.”

Shreeman went on to clarify that there has been no discussion in the organization regarding the team’s disbandment. “I don’t understand how people are already making assumptions about it. Maybe you’ve heard something from somewhere, but I have no idea. Personally, I haven’t heard anything directly suggesting that our lineup is going to change.”

Finally, he confirmed that Team Apex Gaming will be competing in Chennai Esports Global Championship 2026 (CEGC 2026 ) with its active roster and there will be no changes. “We also have a major tournament ongoing. It’s a month-long tournament, and we’ll be competing in it with the same players.”

title: LCS : Team Liquid et LYON se disputent Ackerman
content:
Le mercato s’accélère outre-Atlantique. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Gabriel Agustin « Ackerman » Aparicio serait dans le viseur de Team Liquid et LYON pour la saison prochaine. Les deux organisations auraient entamé des discussions avec le support de LØS, dont le contrat arrive à expiration le 16 novembre. Pour l’instant, aucune décision n’aurait été prise concernant sa future destination.

Arrivé chez LØS en janvier dernier, l’Argentin sort de la meilleure saison de sa carrière. Après une finale lors du premier split du CBLOL, il a décroché le titre lors du Split 2 en dominant FURIA (3-2), devenant le premier joueur latino-américain à remporter le championnat brésilien. Une performance suivie d’un parcours historique aux Worlds 2026, où LØS a notamment éliminé Team Liquid avant de s’incliner aux portes des quarts de finale face à LYON (1-2).

Les deux formations intéressées connaissent donc particulièrement bien le joueur. Sacré champion du Summer Split 2026, Team Liquid a connu une campagne mondiale décevante, avec une élimination dès le Swiss Stage. L’arrivée potentielle d’Ackerman soulèverait notamment la question de l’avenir de CoreJJ, support emblématique de l’organisation depuis huit ans et sept fois champion d’Amérique du Nord sous ses couleurs.

De son côté, LYON a remporté le Lock-In et le Spring Split cette année, avant de s’incliner face à Team Liquid en finale du Summer. L’équipe emmenée par Inspired a ensuite atteint les quarts de finale des Worlds, une première dans son histoire. Reste désormais à savoir laquelle de ces deux formations parviendra à convaincre Ackerman, qui pourrait bientôt franchir une nouvelle étape dans sa carrière.

title: GTA 6 Gameplay Clip Is So Real Fans Think It's Miami
content:
Is this GTA 6, or a phone video from Miami? A new clip shared by Rockstar Games has fans doing a double take, and it is easy to see why.

Posted on IG by Rockstar Games & OnlyInDade https://t.co/ltYMOMtnmw

The clip shows a drive down Vice City's version of Ocean Drive. It runs about 20 seconds and is shot from a first-person view, like a video filmed from the passenger seat of a moving car. Palm trees, pedestrians, buildings and traffic fill the street. That is exactly why people are fooled.

Only in Dade, an Instagram account that posts videos from around Miami, put the clip up. Rockstar Games then shared it on its own Instagram Story. Kotaku reports that Rockstar also liked the original post.

Plenty of viewers could not. Try it yourself. Below are six photos. Some are real places in Miami and Florida. Some are official Rockstar screenshots of GTA 6. Pick which is which.

Vice City is Rockstar's take on Miami, and Leonida is its take on Florida. The clip appears to recreate a viral video from October. In that video, Rockstar and West Coast Customs took custom cars to the streets of Miami to promote GTA 6. The new footage puts the same kind of shots inside Vice City, so the two are easy to confuse.

title: Who Could Replace Jensen Huang? Colette Kress, Ian Buck and Apple’s Johny Srouji Emerge
content:
Nvidia’s board is deciding who could run the company without Jensen Huang, and a short list of names has started to form. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is the leading option for an interim role, after Semafor reported that some directors favour appointing her if Huang is removed. Ian Buck, the Nvidia vice president who invented CUDA, is the internal engineer most often named for the longer term.

Outside the company, Apple’s chief hardware officer Johny Srouji and Arm chief executive Rene Haas have both been mentioned as possible candidates for the permanent job.

SCOOP: As Nvidia's board prepares to fire Jensen Huang, some members favor appointing CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. https://t.co/3ZYayfzLMw

The board has not announced a decision on Huang’s future. Nvidia’s directors met late on Wednesday 11 November, according to Reuters, and Bloomberg reported that the board is working with an outside search firm to identify potential replacements. Nvidia has not commented on the succession talk, and Huang remains chief executive while the investigation led by former federal prosecutor Joon Kim continues. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it ever since, so any successor would be the first new chief executive in the company’s 33 years.

Kress has been Nvidia’s chief financial officer since 2013, after senior finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft. Investors know her well from more than a decade of earnings calls, in which she has explained Nvidia’s rise from a graphics card maker to the world’s most valuable chip company. That familiarity counts for a lot in a crisis, especially with quarterly results due next week. She would also be the first woman to lead the company.

Her limits as a permanent leader are just as clear. Kress does not have an engineering background, which is why reports describe her as a caretaker rather than a long-term successor. Nvidia’s identity rests on its chips and software, and its next permanent leader will be expected to set the technical direction as Huang has done for three decades. An interim chief executive would buy the board time to run a proper search, which appears to be exactly what it has started doing.

title: Booyah Premier League Season 2: All Six Teams and Owners Named Before Jaipur Auction
content:
Garena has named the six teams and 18 creator-owners for Season 2 of the Booyah Premier League (BPL), its creator cricket league for Free Fire India. The owners will pick their squads at a live auction in Jaipur on 18 November. Garena announced the details on 12 November. The cricket tournament itself is planned for January 2027.

Season 2 switches to 11-a-side matches, up from nine-a-side in the first season. Garena expects the number of creators taking part to rise from 78 to 90. Each team now has three creator-owners instead of two. Garena is also opening the league to gaming creators from outside Free Fire India for the first time.

Each team takes its name from a Free Fire India map or location. Six creators join the ownership groups this season: Mortal, Tonde Gamer, Lokesh Gamer, Aditech, Shreeman Legend and Dynamo Gaming.

Mortal joins Nexterra Nawabs, the defending champions. Nexterra Nawabs won the first season with a 27-run win over Bermuda Blasters in the final. Pavan Advani was the final’s most valuable player, after he scored 100 runs off 35 balls.

Garena said official, creator and fan content from Season 1 drew more than 630 million views. That figure includes over 2,500 videos made by fans. Live streams on the official YouTube channel drew more than 10 million views, the company said. Garena has not published how many people watched the final, or how many unique viewers the league reached.

Vaibhav Das Mundhra, Garena’s head of operations in India, said BPL brings gaming creators together “on the field” of cricket. He said Garena wants the league to become “a fixture” that creators and fans look forward to each year. The tournament will stream on the Free Fire India YouTube channel. Garena has promised an opening ceremony, team anthems, mascots and awards, including the Yellow Cap, Red Cap and MVP.

title: PIC 2026 League Stage Groups Revealed: S8UL and TAG Lead 32 Squads Into the PUBG India Challenge
content:
The League Stage groups for the PUBG India Challenge 2026 are set, with 32 squads split into four groups of eight ahead of the stage’s opening day. KRAFTON India Esports confirmed the draw on 12 November, a day after the Open Qualifiers decided which teams would make it this far. Matches begin at 6:25 pm IST, or 12:55 UTC, on the KRAFTON India Esports YouTube channel . S8UL and Team Apex Gaming are the best-known names in the field, alongside a long list of grassroots squads hoping to use the event as a breakthrough.

The League Stage groups are locked. 32 squads. Four groups. The road to the Grand Finals starts here. Live from 6:25 PM today on KRAFTON INDIA ESPORTS YouTube channel. #PIC2026 #PUBGEsports pic.twitter.com/OkL8JmZjSn

Group A carries the biggest name in the tournament. S8UL, one of India’s best-known esports and creator organisations, have been drawn alongside Frog Fusion, CRQ, Team Division, POG, C4, R4 and YKS. Group D includes Team Apex Gaming, the organisation that signed chess grandmaster Vidit Gujrathi as its first chess player earlier this week. Most of the other squads are smaller teams from India’s PUBG PC community, which has had few big stages in recent years.

Group B brings together TVA, HAVK, STA, UKI, BT, TZ, Akatsuki and Dark Squad, while Group C features OR, TOG, Zawlbuk, ORK, Outrage, JINX, Flawless and Agni Crew. The top 12 teams across the stage qualify directly for the Grand Finals, which makes consistency over the whole stage more important than one big night. The Grand Finals on 28 and 29 November will feature 16 teams over 10 matches, played in TPP squads on PUBG: Battlegrounds. The event, organised by KRAFTON with Tesseract Esports, carries a ₹25 lakh prize pool , with ₹7.5 lakh for the champions and a ₹50,000 bonus for the Grand Finals MVP.
