title: Nvidia Hires Former Top Prosecutor Joon Kim and Wachtell Lipton to Lead the Jensen Huang Investigation
content:
Nvidia’s independent directors have hired Joon H. Kim and the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead their investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang. Kim is a former acting US Attorney for the Southern District of New York. The one-line statement from the independent members of the Nvidia board was issued at 14:07 ET (19:07 UTC) on 10 November, through GlobeNewswire .

It says Kim and his firm will carry out the “thorough and independent investigation” that the board first announced on Sunday. The New York Times then reported the hiring as breaking news at 19:31 UTC, and described the inquiry as an investigation into Huang’s affair with a Chinese executive.

Breaking News: Nvidia has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to help lead an investigation into its CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang. https://t.co/gcFqS6el8X

The board had not named its lawyers when it opened the inquiry on 8 November, the day Huang admitted to an affair in a letter to staff. In its first statement , the board said it was looking into reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. It added that it had “no reason to believe” that national security or Nvidia’s secrets had been compromised. The Wall Street Journal reported that Wachtell will examine whether Nvidia was the target of a foreign espionage effort, citing the company.

Kim led the federal prosecutor’s office in Manhattan after Preet Bharara was fired in March 2017, serving as acting US Attorney until early 2018. He later co-led the 2021 independent investigation for New York Attorney General Letitia James into sexual harassment allegations against Governor Andrew Cuomo. That inquiry concluded that Cuomo had sexually harassed multiple women, which he denied, and he resigned within weeks of its publication. His record spans one of the busiest federal prosecutor’s offices in the country and a high-profile inquiry into a powerful man’s personal conduct.

Wachtell is one of the best-known boardroom law firms in the US, and its founding partner Martin Lipton devised the “poison pill” takeover defence in the 1980s. Hiring a former prosecutor from such a firm gives the board an investigator with standing in Washington and on Wall Street. The board has not said how long the inquiry will take, or whether its findings will be made public. Nvidia has also not said whether Huang will step back from any duties while the investigation runs. The decision on his future ultimately sits with the 11 Nvidia directors, whom The Information profiled on Tuesday as the people who must decide whether he stays on.

title: All’s Fair in Love and War, but Not on Wall Street: Nvidia’s $452 Billion Huang Discount
content:
All may be fair in love and war, but the stock market keeps its own score, and on Tuesday it marked Nvidia down again. The chipmaker’s shares were trading at $167.87 on the Nasdaq at 19:28 UTC (14:28 ET) on 10 November, down 6.04% on the day, after a 4.27% fall on Monday. Together, the two sessions since Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a letter to staff had wiped about $452 billion off Nvidia’s market value by that point. That is the biggest loss of company value tied to a chief executive’s personal conduct that TalkEsport has been able to find.

For scale, Hewlett-Packard lost about $9 billion of market value in a day when Mark Hurd resigned as its chief executive in August 2010, after an inquiry into his dealings with a contractor. Nvidia’s two-day loss is about 50 times that, and roughly 24 times the combined losses in all four of the other cases we compared. The figure multiplies the 24.1 billion shares in Nvidia’s latest quarterly filing by the fall from Friday’s close of $186.64. It is a TalkEsport calculation rather than an exchange figure, and it does not assume that every dollar of the fall is down to the scandal.

This is TalkEsport market analysis, not investment advice. Tuesday’s figures are intraday prices at 19:28 UTC (14:28 ET), before the US close, and earlier figures are Nasdaq closing prices.

Corporate history has plenty of chief executives who left under a cloud, but few of those exits cost shareholders more than a few billion dollars. McDonald’s fell about 2.7% when it fired Steve Easterbrook in November 2019 over a consensual relationship with an employee, a drop worth about $5.2 billion on Bloomberg data reported at the time. Wynn Resorts shed about $3.5 billion over two sessions in January 2018 after allegations of sexual misconduct against Steve Wynn, which he denied, according to Fortune. CBS lost more than $1 billion in a day in July 2018, when news broke that The New Yorker was about to publish allegations against Les Moonves, who denied them.

Percentages tell a more modest story, and that matters for anyone reading the chart. Nvidia’s two-day fall of 10.1% is close to HP’s 8% drop in 2010, and well short of the 18% decline CNN reported for Wynn Resorts by early February 2018. The dollar figure is so large because Nvidia is so large, and on Friday it was still worth about $4.5 trillion. Every 1% move in its shares is now worth about $40 billion, more than HP, McDonald’s, Wynn and CBS lost combined. Huang’s own 811.5 million shares, the holding reported by 24/7 Wall St, had lost about $15.2 billion in value by Tuesday afternoon.

The cleaner test is what Nvidia did while the rest of its sector went up. On Monday, the Nasdaq Composite rose 2.7% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index jumped 6.9%, with Broadcom up 8.8% and AMD up 13.3%. Nvidia, the biggest chipmaker in that index by market value, fell 4.27% on the same day. On Tuesday, a hotter-than-expected inflation report pulled the market lower, and by 14:28 ET Nvidia’s 6.04% fall was about 6 times the Nasdaq’s 1.06% decline.

title: Fluxo W7M Pauses Its CS2 Team Over Valve’s Major Changes, TACO Says the Org Made Mistakes Too
content:
Fluxo W7M has paused its Counter-Strike 2 division and released most of its team, ending, at least for the time being, more than four years in the game. The Brazilian organisation confirmed the decision in an official statement on X at 16:33 UTC on 10 November, or 13:33 in Brasília.

It blamed recent changes to “the format and remuneration model” of the CS Majors, combined with the loss of a strategic partner it called fundamental to the operation. Fluxo described the move as a difficult decision “to pause and re-evaluate” its place in the game, according to a TalkEsport translation of the Portuguese statement.

COMUNICADO OFICIAL! pic.twitter.com/vGOXRe3KEq

Players exit and dav1deuS, along with coach juve, remain under contract with Fluxo W7M, the statement says. The rest of the squad will have their contracts ended and are free to negotiate with other teams straight away. Reports of the decision first surfaced about two and a half hours earlier, when journalists from Dust2 Brazil said Fluxo would bench and release its players. The Chilean dav1deuS only joined Fluxo this year, after RED Canids moved its entire roster to the bench in April.

Fluxo did not spell out which Major changes it meant, but Valve overhauled Major stickers for IEM Cologne 2026, replacing sticker capsules with a shop that uses dynamic pricing. Sticker sales have long been one of the biggest sources of income for teams that reach a Major. The business outlet The Esports Radar reported that missed Major revenue, lower sticker earnings and the exit of a commercial partner over Brazil’s betting rules led Fluxo to freeze the project. Fluxo also failed to qualify for PGL Major Singapore, according to the same report.

The statement admitted that results had not always matched expectations. “It was not always the results our fans hoped for, and that we ourselves were seeking,” the organisation wrote. It still pointed to years of competing among Brazil’s top teams, several titles and qualification for three Majors. The lineup changed often along the way, as when Fluxo benched nicks to add mlhzin in March 2025.

title: Amazon’s Ring Now Has a $250 Drone That Patrols Your Home on Its Own
content:
Amazon’s Ring has unveiled a flying security camera that patrols the inside of a home on its own, six years after it first showed a drone that never went on sale. The Ring Drone Cam costs $249.99 and is due to ship to customers in the United States on 27 January 2027, Amazon said in its official announcement on 10 November.

Alongside it, Ring revealed the Rover Cam, a $999.99 wheeled robot that drives to the scene when an alarm goes off. The two devices launch a product line called Ring Robotics, which Amazon describes as “a new category of autonomous, mobile security”.

Amazon shared the announcement on X at 13:38 UTC on 10 November, which was 05:38 Pacific time. Jamie Siminoff, Ring’s founder and chief inventor, said the thinking behind the robots was that “the honest answer wasn’t more cameras”, and that it “meant reimagining what a security device could be”. Posts that spread quickly on X on Tuesday described both machines as home security robots.

Amazon’s own material, however, presents the Rover Cam as a robot for businesses, while only the Drone Cam is meant for homes.

Drone Cam is an indoor camera that rests in a dock out of sight, where it powers down with its camera switched off. Owners can send it along custom routes on a schedule or launch it on demand from the Ring app, and it starts recording only when a flight begins. If a Ring camera, sensor or alarm is triggered, the drone flies by itself to preset patrol points to look into what happened. It records 2K video with a 148-degree field of view, can rotate through 360 degrees and switches on two LED lights in low light.

Both robots run on a system Ring calls AI Pilot, which combines their cameras, vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing. According to Amazon, it maps the space, recognises rooms and suggests patrol points such as side doors, windows and long corridors, and owners can add their own. The drone also works with Alexa Home Map and with Ring’s doorbells, cameras, sensors and alarms. Amazon openly says the propellers are not quiet, so the drone is unlikely to patrol a room unnoticed.

title: GTA 6’s 30fps Reveal Has Players Fuming, but it’s not Rockstar’s first
content:
Rockstar Games has told players exactly what to expect from Grand Theft Auto VI on consoles, and many of them do not like the answer. In a Newswire post published as pre-loading opened on 10 November, the studio said the game is “targeting 30 frames per second” on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar said that target lets it push “both platforms to their absolute limits” while keeping the density of Leonida’s streets and crowds.

We covered the full feature list in our breakdown of the 30fps reveal and the PS5 Pro upgrades , which add PSSR upscaling and ray-traced shadows. The reaction since then has become one of the loudest arguments of the game’s launch week.

Grand Theft Auto VI pre-loading is now available for everyone who has pre-ordered. If you still have yet to pre-order, now’s the time to make sure you're prepared for November 19: https://t.co/LUoPLobocD pic.twitter.com/TLtJUSFBwN

The news spread fastest through accounts that simply repeated it to millions of followers. A summary of the specs posted by DiscussingFilm at 14:09 UTC had passed 42,000 likes and 2.9 million views by the evening, and IGN’s breaking post passed a million views. Rockstar’s own pre-load announcement on X, posted at 13:59 UTC, or 8:59am in New York, drew more than 2,500 replies. Its Newswire post makes no mention of a performance mode, and Rockstar had added nothing on frame rate by 19:00 UTC.

Some of the sharpest criticism came from well-known creators. Gaming YouTuber ExoGhost wrote that he had cancelled his pre-order , calling 30fps in 2026 “unacceptable”. A post from the account Delta169, which passed 8,900 likes, mocked PS5 Pro owners who had expected 60fps and “even begged for a 40fps mode”. The account QNDZY went further, suggesting without evidence that Rockstar is holding back 60fps to sell it as a new feature on a future PS6.

Expectations have changed a great deal since Rockstar’s last major console launch. When GTA V arrived on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S in March 2022, it came with a Performance Mode that “targets 60-FPS”, according to Take-Two’s announcement at the time. Sony also sells the PS5 Pro on the promise that compatible games can be played “at 60fps, or up to 120fps”, as its official PS5 Pro page puts it. Many buyers picked up that console with GTA 6 in mind, as our guide to whether a used PS5 Pro is worth $1,400 for GTA 6 shows. Rockstar’s post promises Pro owners sharper images and better shadows, but it does not mention a higher frame rate.

title: Logitech’s Game Day, Employees get a day off to play GTA 6
content:
Logitech is giving every one of its employees a day off to play video games, in a new company perk it has named Game Day. The Swiss-American company announced the scheme on 10 November in a press release from its twin headquarters in Lausanne and San Jose, describing it as the first company-wide gaming day in its history. Its gaming brand, Logitech G, followed at 18:30 UTC, or 10:30 in San Jose, with a post saying the day is “officially on the calendar”.

The company says the perk recognises “the value of gaming in the workplace and in career development”, rather than treating it as a guilty pleasure.

Every Logitech employee is getting a day off to play games. It’s called Game Day and it’s officially on the calendar. Learn more: https://t.co/feKmVsmGAy pic.twitter.com/Ld52UrnNaO

Chief executive Hanneke Faber framed the move as a challenge to an old prejudice. “It’s time to retire the stereotype that gaming is a waste of time,” she said in the release. Chief people officer Elaine Laird put it even more simply, saying that “play is not the opposite of work”. Robin Piispanen, general manager of Logitech G, said the skills employees sharpen in games, from GTA VI to “shaving seconds off lap times in Forza”, carry over into their jobs.

The release does not set a single date when the whole company logs off, and it does not say how the day will be booked. A dedicated Game Day website says the perk applies to Logitech employees globally, “for the sole purpose of gaming”. It also includes a “Plan your Game Day” calendar of the biggest releases running into 2027, which hints at how staff are expected to use it. Logitech notes that those dates come from publishers and could still change.

Grand Theft Auto VI tops that list as the “Headliner”, with its 19 November launch on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It is joined by Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV on 3 December, the full release of Path of Exile 2 on 11 December and Playground Games’ Fable on 23 February 2027. Rockstar’s game is already the most anticipated of the lot, with an estimated 9.69 million GTA 6 pre-orders tracked by Sensor Tower. Owners can now pre-load GTA 6 , so many will be ready to play the moment it unlocks.

title: Fluxo W7M pauses CS2 operations while keeping exit, dav1deuS, and Juve under contract
content:
Brazilian organization Fluxo W7M failed to qualify for PGL Major Singapore 2026 … and has consequently been forced to suspend its Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) operations for the time being. The org will keep Raphael "exit" Lacerda, David "dav1deuS" Tapia, and coach Gustavo "Juve" Alexandre under contract while management decides what to do next. It's pretty big news for a club that spent four years as a regular in South American CS, though it won’t come as a surprise to everyone.

Fluxo W7M said in a statement that the “current competitive chapter is closing,” and that it will “evaluate future options.”

Why did the org take the decision to take themselves out of the game? Three reasons:

The sticker change isn’t just punishing Fluxo W7M, of course. Indeed, some organizations are seeing earnings plummet sharply by as much as 80% between recent Major cycles. Payouts are said to have dropped from roughly $600,000 to about $120,000, and any clubs that used that money as a cushion big enough to help fund a full year of team operations will now be scrambling around for alternative funding options.

🚨 COMUNICADO OFICIAL! https://t.co/vGOXRe3KEq

Losing partners and smaller sticker payouts are a bit of a perfect storm, with Fluxo W7M one of a few clubs who are stepping back right now. Gaimin Gladiators have gone further and have halted their CS2 project entirely, while Brazilian org ODDIK paused competitive operations indefinitely, leaving their future up in the air.

title: Sentinels Release cortezia and Reduxx as Unrestricted Free Agents, Clearing Cortez for a Return to Brazil
content:
Sentinels have released Gabriel “cortezia” Cortez and Yassin “Reduxx” Aboulalazm as unrestricted free agents, chief executive Rob Moore has confirmed. In a post at 19:05 UTC on 10 November , or 11:05am in Los Angeles, Moore said the club had told both players last week that they would be free to leave. The move means Cortez “will now have the ability to compete and live in Brazil”, according to Moore. He added that both players “lived through a rough 2026 and weren’t able to shine”, and that he looks forward “with some fear” to meeting them in the server again.

Last week we notified that Cortez and Reduxx they would become unrestricted free agents. Cortez will now have the ability to compete and live in Brazil. Both players lived through a rough 2026 and weren’t able to shine. I look forward with some fear to meeting up with them in the…

Moore did not explain the terms, but an unrestricted free agent can usually sign with any team without a transfer fee. That makes both players easy targets in one of the busiest VALORANT off-seasons in years, which our guide to the biggest VCT transfers tracks. Neither Cortez nor Reduxx had commented on X by 19:30 UTC. Fans quickly began linking Cortez with Brazilian teams, although no club has confirmed any talks.

Both players arrived as part of a fresh start that did not work. Sentinels announced Cortez from MIBR in November 2025, after the Brazilian made his top-flight debut that year and helped MIBR reach Masters Toronto and a top-six finish at Champions Paris. Reduxx was a home-grown pick, having been a founding member of the Sentinels academy team before joining the main roster as a sixth player for 2025. He had previously played in North American Challengers for Oxygen Esports in 2023.

The 2026 season went badly almost from the start. Sentinels won one of four matches at VCT Americas Kickoff and finished joint ninth, then finished joint ninth again in Stage 1 after a 2-3 record. The club replaced head coach Kaplan with Ewok, the former RRQ coach, in February, but the change did not turn things around. Sentinels finished joint seventh in Stage 2 and missed both Masters events and Champions, which Vitality and LOUD went on to light up in Shanghai.

Sentinels have rebuilt quickly since the end of the season. The club secured its place as a VCT partner team on 19 October, joining the renewed list of 32 VCT partner teams for 2027 and 2028. On 2 November, it signed the duelist OXY from Cloud9 in a signing post that passed 1.7 million views. The next day it added world champion brawk , before confirming on 4 November that johnqt, the team’s in-game leader, would stay.

title: PUBG Mobile Flash Release Date Confirmed for 13 November
content:
PUBG Mobile Flash, the lighter version of PUBG Mobile, will launch on 13 November, the game’s official account has confirmed. The date first appeared in a post on 9 November that set out the two big releases of the week, listing “PUBG MOBILE Version 4.7” for 12 November and “PUBG MOBILE FLASH” for the following day. PUBG Mobile repeated the Flash date in three more posts on 10 November, describing it as “THE ORIGINAL PUBG MOBILE, NOW IN A FLASH”. Until now, the developer had only confirmed a November launch window for the new app.

Smaller download. Same PUBG MOBILE world. More ways to squad up with your friends! THE ORIGINAL PUBG MOBILE, NOW IN A FLASH. FLASH arrives November 13! Pre-register now on Google Play and the App Store: https://t.co/prr5mODIn8 #PUBGMOBILE #PUBGMFLASH #PUBGMOBILEFLASH #NEWAPP pic.twitter.com/ky48kEUZNb

The confirmation also settles a small mix-up about the date. When Flash first went up for pre-registration, the App Store listing showed an expected date of 12 November, as we noted in our PUBG Mobile Flash download guide . That day now belongs to the version 4.7 update for the main game, which follows the 4.7 beta that opened in September, and Flash follows a day later. PUBG Mobile has not announced an exact launch time, so the app may unlock at slightly different times in different regions.

Flash is built around a much smaller first download, rather than a cut-down version of the game. According to its store listing, Erangel comes pre-installed, so players can jump into their first match straight away and download other maps and modes only when they want them. PUBG Mobile says Flash stays part of the “same PUBG MOBILE world”, with the same battle royale experience, friends and updates as the main app. The pitch in its trailer is simple: the “same PUBG MOBILE experience, just faster”.

The launch marketing leans heavily on how much storage space Flash saves. One video posted on 10 November shows a player deleting a photo to make room for PUBG Mobile, before telling viewers that Flash means “less space needed” and “more room for your memories”. Another stitches together quotes from players praising the smaller size on budget and older phones. Flash replaces the name PUBG Mobile Light, which the game used when it was first announced, as we reported when it was renamed in September .

Pre-registration is still open on Google Play and the App Store, through the official PUBG Mobile Flash pre-registration link . PUBG Mobile says players who pre-register will receive rewards when the game launches, although the exact rewards can vary by region. Anyone who signed up while the app was still called PUBG Mobile Light does not need to register again. As always, players should avoid unofficial APK files and download Flash only from the official stores.

title: Shrek 2 Remastered Is Out Now on PS5, Xbox, Switch 2 and PC, Nine Days Before GTA 6
content:
DreamWorks Shrek 2 Remastered is out now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, Nintendo Switch and PC, bringing back the 2004 co-op game 22 years after it first launched. Aspyr, the Austin studio known for ports and remasters, released it on 10 November, and Xbox told fans to “play now” in a post at 19:04 UTC , or 11:04am Pacific.

The remaster costs $29.99, although a 10% launch discount on Steam brings it down to $26.99 until 17 November. It is also one of the last notable releases before GTA 6 arrives on 19 November, and Aspyr has made no secret of that.

I NEED A HERO Shrek and friends are back in DreamWorks Shrek 2 Remastered! Play now: https://t.co/CCyfILMoez pic.twitter.com/k0C2T5blyf

The original Shrek 2 game launched in North America on 4 May 2004, about two weeks before the film opened in US cinemas. Activision published it, and Luxoflux built the PlayStation 2, Xbox and GameCube versions that this remaster is based on. The original PC release was a separate game, developed by KnowWonder with younger players in mind. It went on to sell more than 4 million copies worldwide by early 2005, and its four-hero team play has kept it popular with players who grew up on it. Aspyr also has history with the game, having handled the Mac version of the original two decades ago.

According to Aspyr, the game has been rebuilt with improved textures, an enhanced interface and reworked cutscenes. It runs at up to 4K resolution on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Switch 2 in docked mode, while the original Switch misses out on 4K. Two features are completely new: a Photo Mode for capturing scenes and a Cheats Menu that can make the adventure easier.

The journey itself is unchanged, running from Shrek’s swamp to Fiona’s castle in Far Far Away, with Easter eggs from the film along the way. Aspyr has not said what frame rate the remaster targets on consoles, as its announcement does not mention one.

title: Vitality promote Scutt to VALORANT Head Coach for 2027, SLK and Szed to join staff
content:
Team Vitality has promoted Scutt to head coach of its VALORANT team for the 2027 season, filling the role left open when PAL departed two weeks after the Champions grand final. The club announced its finalised coaching staff at 17:17 UTC on 10 November, with SLK moving up to assistant coach. Vitality has also brought in Szed as a performance coach, to help the team “aim for the top” next year. The changes complete the staff around a roster that has already lost its best-known player since the season ended in Shanghai.

Our 2027 coaching staff is finalized We are very excited to share that Scutt will be promoted to Head Coach and SLK to assistant coach for our 2027 Season We would also like to welcome Szed as a Performance Coach to strengthen the team and aim for the top this year pic.twitter.com/l27rii6LZc

Scutt confirmed the move in his own post about 80 minutes later. “Happy to say that I will be taking on a new role for Vitality next season and continuing this incredible journey with the group,” he wrote. He added that he was “extremely fortunate to be joined by two incredible coaches who will bring so much to this team in 2027”. The Irish coach lists Fnatic and BBL Esports among his previous teams, and he worked under PAL throughout Vitality’s run to the 2026 Champions final.

Vitality’s 2026 was the best season in the club’s VALORANT history. The team beat G2 Esports 2-0 to reach the upper bracket final at VALORANT Champions 2026 , with Derke and Jamppi starring on Yoru. It then fought back through the lower bracket for a rematch with LOUD in the grand final in Shanghai on 18 October. LOUD won that best-of-five 3-1, and Scutt wrote afterwards that his players’ work all year had been “deserving of” more.

The departures began within a week of the final. On 24 October, Vitality said farewell to Derke , in a post that passed 840,000 views, the duelist it credited with bringing the club “our first VCT trophy” and its first Champions grand final. Two days later, it thanked PAL “for showing us that the mountains were within reach”, calling him “the key in writing a new chapter for Team Vitality in VALORANT”. Scutt paid his own tribute the same day, writing that working alongside PAL had been “an immense honour”.

By promoting from within, Vitality has kept its VALORANT staff in the hands of people who already know the players and the system. Both Scutt and SLK were described as promoted, which means they were already part of the 2026 set-up that reached the world final. Szed is the only new arrival, and Vitality did not say where Szed has worked before, or how the performance role will be split from the head coach’s. Performance coaches in esports usually focus on routines, communication and the mental side of competition, rather than on drafts and tactics.

title: Cyberpunk 2077 is now on Battle.net with a launch discount
content:
Cyberpunk 2077 is now available on Battle.net, making CD Projekt Red’s RPG the latest outside game to join Blizzard’s PC launcher. Blizzard announced the launch on X at 17:00 UTC on 10 November, telling players it was time to “hit the streets of Night City”. Players can buy the base game or the Phantom Liberty expansion separately, or both together in the Ultimate Edition. The Battle.net version arrives with the free Edgerunners 2 Update already included, along with a short-term launch discount.

Access granted. Time to make your name. Cyberpunk 2077 is out NOW on https://t.co/5FazIksDly . Hit the streets of Night City. Play now: https://t.co/W4SDli19pT pic.twitter.com/j0NRUZjb4y

The move was first revealed at BlizzCon in September, during a panel titled “30 Years of Battle.net With Special Guest CD PROJEKT RED”. According to CD Projekt Red’s announcement , community manager Amelia Korzycka and level design lead Miles Tost appeared on stage to discuss the new partnership. Cyberpunk 2077 follows The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered, which CD Projekt Red brought to Battle.net in September. The partnership also covers crossovers with Overwatch and Diablo IV, which are due next year.

On the US Battle.net store , the Ultimate Edition is listed at $31.99 and the base game at $17.99. Blizzard describes those as introductory offer prices, valid until 16 November, and says the price “will increase” after that date. Playing requires the Battle.net desktop app, a Battle.net account and an internet connection, according to the store page. It also notes that the new update “will be available on Mac at a later date”.

The Ultimate Edition bundles the base game with Phantom Liberty, the spy-thriller expansion that launched in September 2023. Phantom Liberty sends V to Dogtown, a walled-off district of Night City, and adds a new story alongside Idris Elba’s character, Solomon Reed. It arrived with the major 2.0 overhaul, which rebuilt the game’s skills, police and combat systems. That update did much to repair the game’s reputation after its troubled launch in December 2020, particularly on older consoles.

The launch includes Update 2.5, which CD Projekt Red calls the Edgerunners 2 Update. It reached PC, PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on 22 October, two days after the anime series Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 premiered on Netflix, according to CD Projekt Red . The update adds a quest featuring Weak “King” Kingsley, one of the new show’s main characters, plus his coat, glasses and revolver. It also brings a radio station with 16 tracks from both Edgerunners series, and the free Witcher 3 themed gear we covered at launch.

title: Alice Huang Linked to Shanghai Firm That Moved $7.5 Billion of Nvidia Chips Into China, Report Says
content:
Alice Huang, the woman US intelligence reportedly believes was gathering information for China, has been linked to a second company that helped move at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia chips into China since 2023. That is the central claim of a report by The Information , published at 10:41 UTC on 10 November, which names the company as Shanghai Century Litong.

According to the report, her relationship with Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang dates back to at least 2023. The publication says the rapport between them helped facilitate those chip sales, a figure far larger than previous estimates.

SCOOP: We find out how long Alice Huang has known Jensen Huang, and identified her real company, Shanghai Century Litong, which enabled at least $7.5B Nvidia chips sales to China since 2023, bigger than previously reported. via @theinformation $NVDA pic.twitter.com/sKlfoyruC3

The figure is more than three times the roughly $2 billion of Nvidia processors that Megaspeed, the Singapore firm where Alice Huang was an executive, was first reported to have bought. The Information’s executive editor, Amir Efrati, wrote on X that her role at Megaspeed was “almost a distraction”. “The real story is her role at China-based Shanghai Century Litong,” he wrote, describing a company that became a “preferred” Nvidia cloud partner in mid-2023. He added that it had facilitated more than $7.5 billion in chip shipments, “incl securing BANNED chips”.

The full article sits behind The Information’s paywall, but outlets that have read it have described its main findings. According to Techzine, the report says Shanghai Century Litong was founded in June 2023 and became a preferred Nvidia cloud partner by that October, which gave it priority in chip allocations. One of its founding shareholders was reportedly linked to Alice Huang’s sister, and that shareholder stepped down in 2024. The report also says Alice Huang kept her own role vague and avoided leaving a paper trail.

The shipments are said to include about 240,000 chips, mostly H100 and H200 accelerators with a small number of A100s. Some of that hardware was subject to US export restrictions on China, according to the report. The A100 and H100 have been covered by US export controls on China since October 2022, which is why their route into the country matters. Century Litong reportedly leased computing power and ran data centres with the chips, serving Chinese technology companies and AI labs. The report also describes links between Century Litong, Megaspeed and a Malaysian subsidiary of Megaspeed.

title: Worlds 2026 : Bin prévient Gen.G avant la finale
content:
Bilibili Gaming n’est plus qu’à une victoire du titre mondial. En dominant T1 (3-1) dimanche à Allen, au Texas, la formation chinoise a réalisé un exploit historique, mettant fin à treize années d’invincibilité des triples champions du monde en titre face aux équipes de la LPL en BO5 aux Worlds. Une performance qui a particulièrement marqué Chen « Bin » Ze-Bin, interrogé sur scène après la rencontre. « C’est un moment historique pour moi. J’ai toujours rêvé de me tenir sur une scène d’une telle envergure face à un joueur aussi mythique que Faker et une équipe du calibre de T1, et de pouvoir arracher cette victoire finale contre eux. Je suis vraiment honoré et très heureux » , a confié le toplaner chinois.

Mais pour Bin, cette qualification ne représente qu’une étape supplémentaire vers son véritable objectif. Malgré les désillusions accumulées ces dernières années, notamment lors des grandes échéances internationales, le joueur refuse de laisser son équipe se satisfaire d’une simple place en finale. « Nous avons fait face à des obstacles et connu des échecs sur notre parcours, mais il est hors de question d’abandonner. Nous allons garder le cap pour atteindre notre but final » , a-t-il assuré. Une détermination qui reflète parfaitement le parcours de BLG, déjà vainqueur de Hanwha Life lors du Swiss Stage, puis de Dplus KIA et T1 en playoffs.

Pour décrocher le trophée, Bilibili Gaming devra toutefois franchir un dernier obstacle, et pas des moindres. Gen.G, champion de la LCK, attend les Chinois en grande finale le 14 novembre prochain à New York. Une affiche qui promet notamment un duel particulièrement attendu sur la toplane entre Bin et Kim « Kiin » Gi-in. Le joueur de BLG n’a d’ailleurs pas hésité à interpeller directement son futur adversaire : « J’ai toujours pensé qu’il était un toplaner très fort. Pour être honnête, lors du First Stand, je voulais l’affronter sur scène, mais malheureusement ils ont été éliminés. Cette fois, c’est l’opportunité pour moi. Alors Kiin, pour cet affrontement en finale, je ne te laisserai pas t’échapper. »

Déjà finaliste à deux reprises sur la scène mondiale, Bin espère enfin soulever le trophée lors de sa troisième tentative. Et après avoir éliminé trois représentants de la LCK, le Chinois ne semble absolument pas impressionné par la perspective d’affronter Gen.G, pourtant invaincu en playoffs après deux victoires 3-0. « Nous avons déjà battu trois équipes de la LCK durant notre parcours et Gen.G nous attend désormais. Nous n’allons pas manquer cette opportunité. Nous allons rentrer chez nous en tant que champions » , a-t-il lancé avec assurance. Une déclaration ambitieuse qui donne déjà le ton d’une finale explosive entre les deux meilleures équipes de ces Worlds 2026.

THE #WORLDS2026 FINAL: @BilibiliGaming versus @GenG ! pic.twitter.com/DSSoqnn8oN

title: Marvel Posts a Binary Code Message Before the VisionQuest Finale… We’ve it decoded
content:
Marvel Studios has posted a message written entirely in binary code, hours before the finale of VisionQuest, and fans have already cracked it. The post on X , published at 17:00 UTC on 10 November, consists of 55 groups of eight ones and zeros. Read as standard ASCII text, it spells out a single line, “We could never truly leave each other, even if we tried”, and nothing else. The post had passed 970,000 views within a few hours, and Marvel has not explained who is speaking or to whom.

01010111 01100101 00100000 01100011 01101111 01110101 01101100 01100100 00100000 01101110 01100101 01110110 01100101 01110010 00100000 01110100 01110010 01110101 01101100 01111001 00100000 01101100 01100101 01100001 01110110 01100101 00100000 01100101 01100001 01100011 01101000…

The timing points straight at VisionQuest , the Disney+ series that concludes the trilogy that began with WandaVision in 2021 and continued with Agatha All Along in 2024. An hour before the binary post, the same account shared a clip captioned “VISIONQUEST PROGRAM: FINALIZING”, reminding fans that the season finale streams at 6pm Pacific Time on 10 November. That is 02:00 UTC on 11 November, and the message reads like a line of dialogue lifted from the episode. This article contains no spoilers for the finale, which had not been released at the time of writing.

Each group of eight digits in the post is one byte, and each byte stands for a single character. The first group, 01010111, converts to the number 87, which is a capital W in the ASCII table that computers have used for decades. The next, 01100101, is the number 101, a lower-case e, and 00100000 is the number 32, which is a space. Working through all 55 groups in the same way produces the full sentence, comma included, with no hidden second layer that fans have found so far. Anyone can check it with a free binary-to-text converter, or by hand with an ASCII chart.

Binary is a natural choice for a show about a synthetic being. In VisionQuest, the rebooted Vision searches for his humanity by consulting the artificial intelligences in his own programming, including J.A.R.V.I.S., F.R.I.D.A.Y., E.D.I.T.H. and Ultron. Marvel has leaned into that idea throughout its campaign, with promotional posts styled as system messages and loading screens. The series also leans on Marvel’s history of synthetic heroes, including Jim Hammond, the original Human Torch, whom VisionQuest reimagines. Its finale event write-up carried the heading “FINAL SEQUENCE LOADING”.

Fans have offered several readings of the line, and Marvel has not confirmed any of them. Accounts devoted to the Scarlet Witch were among the first to quote the post, reading it as a message between Vision and Wanda Maximoff. Elizabeth Olsen has not been confirmed for VisionQuest, and showrunner Terry Matalas has declined to say whether Wanda appears. Wanda’s apparent death in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness was never shown on screen, which has kept that theory alive. Olsen has not played the character on screen since that 2022 film.

title: BGMI Air: Launch Date, Size, Beta, and All We Know
content:
If your phone groans every time BGMI asks for another resource pack, this one’s for you. BGMI Air is KRAFTON India’s lighter version of Battlegrounds Mobile India. It launches on December 10, 2026, and the first download is only about 1GB.

Below is everything KRAFTON has actually confirmed, what’s only been reported, and what nobody knows yet. Those three things are not the same, and a lot of coverage blurs them.

If you pre-registered for “BGMI Lite” back in August, you signed up for this same game. KRAFTON just changed the name.

That jump from 10 million to 14 million came in roughly three weeks, before there was even a release date. Plenty of people clearly have phones that struggle with the main game.

The headline number is the 1GB initial download. KRAFTON says the idea is a smaller download that keeps BGMI’s core gameplay. Reports also say you won’t have to grab extra packs before your first match.

For comparison, regular BGMI can climb to around 8GB once you add its packages, according to ETV Bharat. That gap is the whole point of Air.

title: GTA 6 Is Now the Most Pre-Ordered Game, With Estimated 9.69 Million Copies, Passing Cyberpunk 2077
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has become the most pre-ordered game in the history of both PlayStation Store and Microsoft Store, nine days before it launches. Sony and Microsoft confirmed the records on 10 November, as pre-loading opened on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Market intelligence firm Sensor Tower now estimates that GTA 6 has sold about 9.69 million digital pre-orders across the two consoles, generating roughly $942 million in revenue.

If that estimate is right, Rockstar’s game has passed the 8 million pre-orders that CD Projekt reported for Cyberpunk 2077 in 2020, long regarded as the record.

We're only two weeks away from the biggest game launch of the last decade, GTA VI, as @Rockstargames and #TakeTwoInteractive has shifted ad spend into high gear over the last 30 days. Check out our exclusive #GTAVI pre-order and revenue sales tracker across @PlayStation and… pic.twitter.com/aBOoiDcjlp

Sony made its announcement in a PlayStation Blog post published at 15:41 UTC on 10 November. “Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store,” wrote Tim Turi, a content communications manager at Sony Interactive Entertainment. Microsoft used similar language on Xbox Wire , calling GTA 6 “the most pre-ordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store”. Neither company gave a figure, and Rockstar and Take-Two have not published pre-order numbers either.

The 9.69 million figure comes from Sensor Tower’s GTA VI Sales Tracker , which was last updated on 10 November. It counts estimated digital sales on PlayStation and Xbox, net of returns, so cancelled pre-orders and refunds have been taken out. By Sensor Tower’s numbers, PS5 accounts for 7.23 million copies and $703 million, while Xbox Series X|S accounts for 2.46 million copies and $239 million. That puts the platform split at 75% to 25%, almost exactly where it was a week ago.

The pace has picked up sharply in the final stretch. Sensor Tower’s snapshot for 3 November had GTA 6 at about 7.71 million pre-orders and $751 million, as we reported when pre-orders passed $750 million . That means close to 2 million copies were added in a single week, worth about $191 million in revenue. The revenue estimate also works out at roughly $97 per copy, closer to the $99.99 Ultimate Edition than the $79.99 standard edition, although the public tracker does not split sales by edition.

title: Overwatch Brings Back 6v6 Role Queue in a Four-Week Competitive Mini Season for Season 6
content:
Overwatch is bringing back 6v6 Role Queue for Competitive play, as a four-week test that starts on the first day of Season 6. Game director Aaron Keller confirmed the “2-2-2 Role Queue Competitive mini season” in a Director’s Take post that Blizzard shared on X at 17:02 UTC on 10 November. The test comes with a dedicated balance patch for 6v6 and matchmaking changes aimed at keeping queues short.

Players will be able to choose between the standard 5v5 Competitive mode, 6v6 Open Queue and the new 6v6 Role Queue. Blizzard did not give a launch date in the post, but Season 5’s final events run until 7 December, and fan site Overwatch Cavalry lists the test for 8 December.

In the latest Director’s Take, Game Director Aaron Keller returns with an update on the state of 5v5 and 6v6 as the Reign of Talon comes to an end https://t.co/G7hg53A2aM pic.twitter.com/UmJg26DmVX

Role Queue locks each team into two tanks, two damage heroes and two supports, the format Overwatch used before it moved to five-player teams. Keller said 6v6 Open Queue has “steadily grown in popularity” and was the second most-played mode in Season 5 , with Mystery Madness close behind. He also admitted that Blizzard had been “a little hesitant” to bring 6v6 Role Queue back, because queue times “could increase significantly”. Two tests earlier this year used different queueing methods, but Keller wrote that neither “really delivered on the promise” players were looking for.

The biggest change is in how Blizzard talks about the two formats. Keller wrote that the team once thought it “might be able to find one format to transition Overwatch to”, but that the community clearly wants several modes instead. He described the game using an amusement park analogy, asking why players should choose “between the roller coaster of 5v5 and the bumper car chaos of 6v6” when they can have both. Blizzard does not intend to move the main mode to 6v6, he added, but now thinks of it as “a second among equals”.

The surveys Blizzard ran after its 6v6 tests show why it has landed there. Asked which version of Quick Play they preferred, 32% of respondents said they much preferred 5v5 and another 32% said they much preferred 6v6 with 2-2-2 Role Queue. Smaller groups somewhat preferred one side or the other, and 12% had no preference at all. Keller said many players also engage with both modes, and that the strength of feeling on each side was the most striking part of the data.

title: “John Wick Meets GTA”: How to Rob a Bank Clip Compares Its Car Chase to Grand Theft Auto Days Before GTA 6
content:
David Leitch’s new heist film How to Rob a Bank has released two clips ahead of its cinema launch this Friday, and one of them name-checks Grand Theft Auto. In a car chase scene called “This is Real Life”, the film’s crew of bank robbers compare their getaway driving to practice in GTA, and conclude that the real thing is “way cooler in real life”.

The comparison helped push “action thriller” into Google’s trending searches in the UK on Tuesday, according to Google Trends . How to Rob a Bank opens in UK and US cinemas on 13 November, six days before GTA 6 itself launches.

The two clips were released by Amazon MGM Studios, which is distributing the film in North America. In the first, viewers ride along in the escape vehicle as the crew attempts a “reverse punch” manoeuvre to shake off pursuing police, according to the film site MovieWeb, which published both clips. The second, titled “The System is Corrupt”, is a tense argument between two characters about why the crew robs banks at all. Sony Pictures is handling the release outside North America, including in the UK and Ireland.

The film follows a crew of social media-savvy bank robbers who broadcast their heists online, and whose growing fame puts them in danger. In the studio’s words, that viral success draws the attention of a veteran FBI agent and a software engineer, while the crew pushes ahead with its most ambitious job yet. Nicholas Hoult plays the crew’s leader, Ryan, alongside Pete Davidson as Vince and Zoë Kravitz as Reagan Gardner. John C. Reilly plays Agent West, and the cast also includes Christian Slater, Tati Gabrielle, Anna Sawai and Rhenzy Feliz.

Leitch is best known for his work on John Wick, which he co-directed with Chad Stahelski in 2014, although only Stahelski received the director’s credit. He has since directed Atomic Blonde, Deadpool 2, Bullet Train and The Fall Guy, and produced the film through his company 87North. Mark Bianculli wrote the screenplay, and the cinematographer Jonathan Sela and editor Elísabet Ronaldsdóttir both return from John Wick. The film runs for 122 minutes, carries an R rating in the US and a 15 certificate in the UK, and was originally due on 4 September before moving to November.

The GTA reference is a natural fit for a film about robbers who treat crime as content. Rockstar’s games have long been built around car chases, police pursuits and heists, and the crew in How to Rob a Bank treat their getaways as something to film and share. Streaming culture is also already wrapped up in GTA, from roleplay servers to the Kai Cenat GTA marathon sets that went viral this month. That makes the “John Wick meets GTA” label used in some coverage of the clips easy to understand.

title: Mobile Legends Studio Moonton Moves Closer to Saudi Ownership After China’s Unconditional Approval
content:
China’s competition regulator has cleared Savvy Games Group’s purchase of Moonton, the studio behind Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, without attaching any conditions. The State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) completed its review on 29 October, and listed the deal among the mergers it approved unconditionally between 26 October and 1 November. That list was published on SAMR’s website on 6 November, and the approval drew wider attention this week after reports by TechNode and The Esports Advocate. The ruling removes one of the regulatory hurdles facing a deal that values Moonton at more than $6 billion.

Savvy, which is wholly owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), agreed to buy Moonton from ByteDance in March. Neither company has disclosed the final price, but Skadden, which advised ByteDance , described it as “reported to be above $6 billion”. The sale has not yet closed, and no closing date has been announced. Savvy and ByteDance had not commented on the Chinese approval by Tuesday evening, UTC.

The SAMR notice does not use Savvy’s brand name. According to The Esports Advocate, it lists the buyer as Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company, the Riyadh entity that owns the Savvy trademark, and the targets as Moonton Holdings Limited and Shanghai Moonton Technology. An unconditional approval means the regulator found no competition concerns that needed remedies, such as asset sales or limits on how the business is run. Chinese approval was always going to be required, because Moonton’s operating company and headquarters are in Shanghai.

Skadden said in March that closing depended on customary conditions, including certain regulatory approvals. It did not list which authorities were involved, and neither company has said whether any other reviews are still open. The timetable has already stretched further than Savvy first suggested. When it confirmed the agreement, Savvy said it expected the deal to close “in the coming months”.

The sale has been building for most of the year. Reuters reported in February that ByteDance was in advanced talks to sell Moonton to Savvy for $6 billion to $7 billion, and the two sides announced an agreement on 20 March, according to Arab News . ByteDance had bought Moonton through its gaming arm Nuverse in 2021, at a valuation of about $4 billion. The Chinese company has since pulled back from large parts of its games business.

Savvy chief executive Brian Ward said in March that the deal “directly supports Savvy’s purpose to enable prosperity and connection through play for generations to come”. He added that, once completed, it would “further strengthen our leadership in mobile games”. Moonton chief executive Zhang Yunfan is expected to stay on after closing, and an internal letter seen by Reuters said the management structure would remain unchanged. According to Savvy, Mobile Legends has more than 110 million monthly players and more than 1.5 billion installs worldwide.

title: Overwatch tests 6v6 Role Queue Competitive mode in Season 6
content:
Overwatch will get a six-versus-six (6v6) Role Queue Competitive mode in Season 6. Here’s what game director Aaron Keller said about it and more.

Overwatch’s 6v6 Competitive Role Queue will be a ranked mini season launching on Day 1 of Season 6. It will also run for four weeks. The game’s existing 6v6 Open Queue will keep running as well, with the balance patch applied to both game modes.

“There will be three Competitive options of the game available on Day 1 of Season 6: our standard 5v5, Open Queue 6v6, and our Role Queue 6v6 test.” Keller stated. “The 2-2-2 Role Queue Competitive mini season will start at season launch and run for the first four weeks of the season.”

Overwatch’s 6v6 mode has been gaining popularity over the last few years. There’s always been a debate between five-versus-five (5v5) and 6v6 as well. However, the developers have come to the realization that there doesn’t have to be a “winner” between 5v5 and 6v6 at all. Both formats can coexist and cater to different player preferences.

Earlier this year, the Overwatch team ran a couple of tests to explore different ways of bringing Role Queue to 6v6, but neither test quite delivered the experience players were looking for in the game mode.

The Overwatch surveys that went out after these two tests also revealed interesting details about player preferences. It showed that 32% of respondents strongly favored their own format of choice. Therefore, instead of selecting one format to transition Overwatch to, the game will feature both of them.

title: LEC : Fnatic vise Supa et Aetinoth
content:
Le mercato continue de s’accélérer en LEC, et Fnatic compte bien jouer les premiers rôles. Selon les informations du média espagnol Esportmaníacos , les Orange et Noir auraient entamé des discussions avec David « Supa » García et Berat « Aetinoth » Tıknazoğlu en vue de la saison 2027. Deux profils très différents, mais qui pourraient permettre à l’organisation britannique de renforcer considérablement sa botlane. Le premier possède déjà une solide expérience au plus haut niveau européen, tandis que le second fait partie des jeunes talents les plus prometteurs des ligues régionales.

À 26 ans, Supa sort d’une belle saison sous les couleurs de Movistar KOI. L’ADC espagnol a notamment décroché une place sur le podium du LEC Versus et du Spring Split, avant d’atteindre la finale du Summer Split, perdue face à G2 (0-3) à Nice. Sur la scène internationale, KOI s’est également illustré lors des Worlds 2026 avec des victoires face à Bilibili Gaming, futur finaliste, et aux Taïwanais de CTBC Flying Oyster. Son parcours s’est finalement arrêté aux portes des quarts de finale, après une défaite contre la Karmine Corp (0-2). Des performances qui ont visiblement attiré plusieurs prétendants, puisque Vitality et NAVI seraient également intéressés par le joueur espagnol.

L’autre piste mène directement en LFL. À seulement 21 ans, le Turc Aetinoth a réalisé une saison 2026 remarquable avec Solary, l’une des formations les plus impressionnantes du circuit européen. Double champion de France et vainqueur des EMEA Masters Winter, l’ADC a largement contribué aux succès de la structure tourangelle. Son équipe a ensuite terminé vice-championne des EMEA Masters au printemps, avant de s’incliner en finale du World Star Challengers Invitational face à T1 Academy (2-3), puis de décrocher une nouvelle médaille d’argent aux EMEA Masters Summer. Un bilan qui pourrait désormais lui ouvrir les portes du LEC.

Pour Fnatic, ces deux pistes témoignent d’une volonté de retrouver les sommets après une saison décevante. La structure britannique s’active sur plusieurs fronts et serait notamment sur le point de recruter Labrov en provenance de G2 Esports, selon les dernières rumeurs. Reste désormais à savoir quel ADC pourrait l’accompagner sur la botlane en 2027. Entre l’expérience de Supa et le potentiel d’Aetinoth, Fnatic dispose de deux options séduisantes, mais la concurrence s’annonce particulièrement rude pour attirer l’Espagnol. Pour l’heure, aucun accord n’a été annoncé avec l’un ou l’autre des joueurs.

As of today, anyone who has already reserved a copy of GTA 6 can start downloading it ahead of launch, so you’re able to dive into the game as soon as it launches.

Initially, Rockstar had scheduled GTA 6 pre-loads for November 12, which is a week before launch. The date was then moved up to November 10th.

Through an X post earlier today, Rockstar confirmed that PS5 pre-loading is now available for everyone who pre-ordered the title.

title: GTA 6 Is Coming to Xbox One, but Only Through the Cloud
content:
GTA 6 is coming to Xbox One after all, but only through the cloud. Rockstar Games has confirmed that the game will be playable through Xbox Cloud Gaming from launch on November 19, and that cloud access is limited to Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S consoles. There is no native Xbox One version, so the game runs on Microsoft’s servers and streams to your console.

For anyone still on a 2013-era Xbox, that is a genuine way in without buying a new console. It also comes with some catches worth knowing before November 19.

Xbox Cloud Gaming runs the game on Microsoft’s servers and sends the picture to your console over the internet. Your Xbox One handles the controls and display, while the hard work happens elsewhere. That is why a console that could never run GTA 6 itself can still play it.

Rockstar says cloud-enabled Xbox games always use Xbox Series S graphics settings, and GTA 6 will too. So Xbox One owners will see roughly what a Series S player sees, at the same 30fps target Rockstar has set for every console, as long as their internet connection keeps up. We covered the 30fps target and the PS5 Pro-only features in more detail when Rockstar announced them.

A strong internet connection: Streaming a game like GTA 6 depends entirely on your connection. A fast, stable line, ideally wired rather than Wi-Fi, will make a big difference to picture quality and input delay.

The right subscription: Rockstar has not said which Game Pass tier GTA 6 cloud play requires, or whether you need to own the game to stream it. GTA 6 is not on Game Pass, so you should expect to need both a copy of the game and a Game Pass plan that includes cloud gaming. Microsoft is also introducing an hourly cloud gaming pass this month, which Xbox Insiders are already testing, according to Windows Central . Whether it covers GTA 6 is not yet clear.

title: Eight Major teams get one last test at BLAST Rivals in Hong Kong
content:

BLAST Rivals Season 2 starts in Hong Kong on Wednesday, and for all eight teams it is the final stop before the PGL Major Singapore . Six of them, MOUZ , Team Vitality , FURIA , Team Spirit , Team Falcons and Legacy , are invited straight to the Major’s Stage 3 on 2 December. G2 Esports and FUT Esports start in Stage 2 on 28 November.

The event runs from 11 to 15 November with $1,000,000 in prize money, $250,000 of it for the winners. The eight teams play in two groups of four, double elimination and Bo3. Group winners go straight to the semi-finals, the second and third-placed teams to the quarter-finals, and the fourth-placed teams go home. The playoffs are played in front of fans at AsiaWorld-Arena, and Sunday’s grand final is a Bo5. Groups, prize money and streams are on our tournament page .

The first series starts on Wednesday 03:00 CET .

Thursday follows the same rhythm: the two opening losers in each group meet in an elimination match, and the two winners play for a semi-final place. The quarter-finals start on Friday 08:00 CET , and the grand final on Sunday 08:00 CET .

Two of the openers come with history. Vitality beat Falcons 3-2 in the first Rivals final in Copenhagen in May 2025, and Falcons lost the Hong Kong final a year ago as well, 3-1 to FURIA. title: GTA 6 Runs at 30fps on Consoles, and PS5 Pro Gets Exclusive Ray-Traced Shadows
content:
GTA 6 will run at 30 frames per second on consoles, Rockstar Games has confirmed. The studio revealed the target in a Newswire post on November 10, the same day pre-loading opened, and said the game was built “from the ground up” for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, pushing both “to their absolute limits”.

Rockstar explains the choice directly. It says the 30fps target lets it bring “the vast and rich world of Leonida to life” while “maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants”. In other words, Rockstar has chosen a busier, more detailed world over a higher frame rate.

That will disappoint some players who have got used to 60fps performance modes on current consoles. However, it is in line with Rockstar’s history. Red Dead Redemption 2 ran at 30fps on consoles when it launched in 2018, and Rockstar’s open worlds have always prioritised detail and density. The post does not mention a performance mode, so for now, 30fps is the only target Rockstar has confirmed.

The PS5 Pro version gets two upgrades that are not available on any other console, according to Rockstar.

PSSR, or PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution, is Sony’s AI upscaling, and Rockstar says it gives the Pro version “improved clarity”. The ray-traced shadows are listed as “only available on PlayStation 5 Pro”.

It is worth being clear about what the post does not say. Rockstar does not mention a higher frame rate on PS5 Pro, so Pro owners should expect a sharper, better-lit game, not a smoother one.

title: Are Sentinels Back? What a 45 Second Cooldown Changes for Cypher, Killjoy and Vyse
content:
Fifteen seconds does not sound like much. In Valorant, it can be the difference between a Sentinel who is useless for the rest of the round and one who is ready to hold the next push. Patch 13.10 cuts the cooldown on Cypher’s Spycam, Killjoy’s Turret and Vyse’s Arc Rose after they are destroyed, from 60 seconds to 45.

So, are Sentinels back? Not quite, and Riot is careful not to say so. But this is the first time in a while that the class has been nudged in the right direction, and it is worth understanding exactly what changes on the server.

Only the destroyed cooldown changes. The abilities themselves, their health, range and effects, are exactly the same. Riot’s own wording in the 13.10 patch notes is that this is “a small, targeted change” while it looks at Sentinel cooldowns more broadly. In other words, it is a test, not a rework.

Riot picked 45 seconds deliberately. It says the new cooldown sits slightly below the 50-second signature cooldown that Initiators have. That comparison tells you what Riot is thinking.

Until now, the trade was lopsided. An Initiator could spend a signature ability to clear a Sentinel’s camera or turret, then get that ability back 10 seconds before the Sentinel got theirs. Now the Sentinel wins that race by five seconds. Breaking a setup still costs the Sentinel, but it no longer leaves them a step behind for most of the round.

Put it against a round. A Valorant round lasts 100 seconds before the Spike is planted, and the Spike itself burns for 45. A utility piece destroyed early in the round now has a realistic chance of coming back before the round ends, either for a retake or for a post-plant.

title: How to Use Replay Bookmarks in Valorant on PC and Console
content:
Valorant patch 13.10 adds replay bookmarks, a simple way to mark a moment during a match so you can jump straight back to it when you watch the replay. It works on both PC and console, but there is one catch on PC: the key is not set by default, so bookmarks will not work until you assign one.

Here is how to set it up on each platform, and how to get the most out of it.

A bookmark is a marker you drop on the match timeline while you are playing. Later, when you open that match’s replay, your bookmarks show up on the timeline so you can skip to those moments instead of scrubbing through the whole game.

Bookmarks are private. According to Riot’s patch 13.10 notes , they are only visible to you and will not appear for anyone else who watches the same replay.

On PC, you need to choose a key before your first match.

Pick a key that does not clash with your abilities, weapons or comms. A spare mouse button or an unused key near your left hand works well, so you can bookmark without taking your eyes off the fight.

title: Valorant Patch 13.10 Notes: Sentinel Buffs, Assist Changes and Replay Bookmarks
content:
Valorant patch 13.10 is out, and the biggest news for ranked players is a set of Sentinel buffs. Cypher’s Spycam, Killjoy’s Turret and Vyse’s Arc Rose now come back 15 seconds faster after being destroyed. The patch also adds replay bookmarks, changes how assists are counted, and gives Gauntlet: Glitched five-player parties and new abilities.

The changes line up with what leaks suggested for 13.10 last week, and Riot has now confirmed them in the official 13.10 patch notes .

Riot says these are “light changes” to encourage more back-and-forth between teams. The idea is to give Sentinels more room to place utility early and reset it mid-round, while still rewarding the team that breaks their setup.

The new 45-second cooldown sits just below the 50-second cooldown on Initiator signature abilities, which Riot points out on purpose. Cypher does lose something too. Picking up his Spycam now takes longer to come back, bringing him in line with other Sentinels.

Riot also calls this “a small, targeted change” while it looks at Sentinel cooldowns more broadly, so bigger changes may follow in a later patch.

title: Apex Legends Legend bans explained: how Ranked voting works
content:
Two Legends are removed from every Diamond lobby in Season 31, and a weighted draw decides which, so even the most voted pick is never a guaranteed ban.

Two bans per match, one request per player and a pool of at least four candidates: those are the numbers behind Legend banning, the Ranked feature that arrived with Apex Legends Season 31, Cipher, on Tuesday 3 November 2026. EA set out the rules in the Cipher patch notes and the reasoning in its Ranked roadmap from 20 October. Here is who gets to vote, when the vote happens, how the draw works and which Legends look most exposed.

Bans follow the lobby, not your own badge. EA has tied the feature to Drop Zone deployment, the high rank format where each squad is assigned a landing spot before Legend select, and its roadmap says any match with Diamond or higher players will use it. EA’s Ranked help page describes Drop Zone matches as lobbies that meet a certain threshold of Diamond, Master and Apex Predator players, and the loading screen tells you when you are in one.

Inside such a match every player has one request, whether you queue solo or in a premade squad. Ranked lobbies that still start from the Dropship have no ban phase, and the feature does not exist outside Ranked.

The ban phase sits at the very start of the match, before anyone picks a Legend:

EA’s help page adds that each player can also signal a Legend they do not want banned. EA has not said how long the request timer runs.

title: Cloud9 Ventures Into Deadlock By Purchasing Melee Creeps
content:
North American esports titan Cloud9 has officially stepped into the competitive Deadlock arena, acquiring the reigning North American juggernaut lineup known as Melee Creeps. Announced on November 9, 2026, via the organization’s newly launched @C9DLock social media channels, the Cloud9 venture into Deadlock brings an undefeated six-player roster and its existing support staff under one of gaming’s most recognizable banners.

For Cloud9, an organization founded in 2012 that famously became the first and only North American squad to capture a Counter-Strike Major title at ELEAGUE Major: Boston 2018, the signing marks a high-profile return to a Valve-developed title. After stepping back from Counter-Strike 2 in January 2025, Cloud9 spent 22 months without a presence in Valve’s competitive ecosystem before making its move into the 6v6 third-person hero-shooter MOBA hybrid.

Rather than piecing together a speculative roster from free agency, Cloud9 opted to sign the entire active Melee Creeps lineup alongside its coaching and managerial structure. All six starting players have inked one-year salaried contracts with Cloud9, though specific salary figures remain undisclosed.

The acquisition is the culmination of months of behind-the-scenes interest. Cloud9 first approached the team around March 2026 to propose a co-branded sponsorship arrangement dubbed MLC x Cloud9 that centered heavily around former player and popular streamer eidorian. Melee Creeps turned down that initial sponsorship pitch, prompting Cloud9 to return later in the year with a full-scale organizational acquisition.

Beyond their tournament pedigree, the players offer immediate livestreaming reach for Cloud9. Trivon “Lomein” Pham has drawn peak concurrent viewership exceeding 2,000 viewers, while teammates Sobhan “AVG” Pirasteh and Isaiah “Saiah” Mendoza regularly attract peaks above 600 and up to 900 concurrent viewers, respectively.

To understand why Cloud9 chose this specific six-man unit, one has to look at the grassroots history of competitive Deadlock . Established in October and November 2024 as an independent, organization-less North American squad, Melee Creeps originally featured a lineup of Saiah, AVG, Braeden, CoolCheese, Opp, and Bam1. While roster turnover is common in pre-release esports scenes, Saiah remained the team’s anchor through multiple iterations, with JonJon joining the starting lineup in April 2025.

title: Latency, Frame Rate and RNG: Three Different Things Players Often Confuse
content:
A shot feels late, the camera stutters and the next attack produces an unexpected damage number. In chat, all three problems might get called lag. That description makes troubleshooting difficult because the symptoms can come from completely different parts of the game.

Latency measures delay. Frame rate describes how frequently frames are produced. Random number generation supplies values that game rules can use to select outcomes. The three can operate during the same action, but they answer different questions.

Network latency concerns communication between machines. A game’s ping counter usually reports an estimate of round-trip time to a server. System latency concerns the local path from an input to the resulting change on the display.

That difference matters when a game feels unresponsive despite a low ping. The delay can involve the input device, game processing, rendering or display. A fast network connection does not remove every step between clicking a mouse and seeing the response.

NVIDIA’s explanation of system and network latency separates these paths and explains why FPS alone cannot measure responsiveness. A useful latency reading must identify the part of the process it measures.

For troubleshooting, describe the symptom first. Does the view turn late when the mouse moves? Does a server-confirmed interaction arrive late while local movement looks smooth? Those observations provide more information than calling both problems lag.

title: Epic Games Claims Ownership of Jazz Jackrabbit Amid Legal Dispute
content:

The veteran video game designer, known for his work with the Gears of War franchise, has claimed that this attempt to regain control of the game, Jazz Jackrabbit, has concluded with the creators of Fortnite retaining its complete rights.
